Dear Sirs/Madam, 
Sub: Preferential Issue of warrants (“Warrants”) convertible into equivalent equity 
shares of face value ₹ 1 each (the “Equity Shares”) by Bajaj Finance Limited (the 
“Company”) to Bajaj Finserv Limited, Promoter and holding company (the 
“Promoter”) under the provisions of Chapter V of the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, 
as amended (the “SEBI ICDR Regulations”) (the “Issue”). 
Ref: Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended   
With reference to intimation pertaining to outcome of Board meeting dated 1 October 
2026 and further to our intimation dated 5 November 2026 intimating about the meeting 
of the PI 2026-Special Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company 
(“Committee”) to be held on 10 November 2026 in respect of the Issue, we wish to inform 
you that the Committee at its meeting held today, i.e. 10 November 2026, has approved 
the issue of 5,74,25,740 (Five Crore Seventy-Four Lakh Twenty-Five Thousand Seven 
Hundred Forty Only) Warrants to the Promoter, at an issue price of ₹ 1,010 (Rupees One

November 5, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
MANAGEMENT: 
MR. HERJIT BHALLA – CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER – INDIA BUSINESS – 
DABUR INDIA LIMITED 
MR. ANKUSH JAIN – CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER – DABUR INDIA LIMITED 
MR. RAHUL SARAWAGI – HEAD, INVESTOR RELATIONS AND M&A – 
DABUR INDIA LIMITED 
 

 
Rahul Sarawagi: 
Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. A very warm welcome to all of you and 
thank you very much for coming to this event and taking the time to join us in 
person. It's a pleasure to have with us our valued investors, analysts, as well as 
members from the financial fraternity. Your continued engagement with Dabur, 
your perspectives and your valuable feedback are always welcome and 
appreciated. Dabur is a company with a rich heritage and a distinctive place in 
India's consumer landscape. Over the years, we have built a business around a 
deep understanding of consumers, a strong connection with our brands, and a 
continued focus on health, wellness, and everyday household needs. 
I'm sure you must have already gone through our Q2 FY27 results. But today, 
this goes a step further. Here, we'll be talking more about what our perspective 
is on our business; what the key focus areas are; how we have progressed; and 
what opportunities lie ahead. Today, over the course of today's session, Mr 
Herjit Bhalla, who is our India Business CEO, will take us through the 
presentation, which will be followed by a Q&A session. With that, I would now 
like to invite Herjit to come on stage and take us through the presentation. 
 
 
Herjit Bhalla: 
Thank you, Rahul. A very good afternoon to all of you. Thank you for being here, 
and in advance, wishing all of you the best for Diwali. So, I'm Herjit Bhalla, and 
I am delighted to be here today to have this conversation with you, to share 
with you how I have seen the last 6 months go, and also to take some insights 
from you on what you guys are thinking as well. So the agenda for the next little 
bit is going to be as follows. We're just going to do a very quick look at Dabur 
as I saw it when I was coming into the organisation, and what I believe I have 
learned in my first 6 months. I'm also going to do a quick assessment of our 
performance and what we're going to be doing next. 
 
 
So, very clearly, you know, it's rare that you join a new organisation and you've 
already been familiar with and using the brands for many decades. That's how 
day one at Dabur felt, right? This is truly an amazing organisation with a very 
rich heritage. We're all aware: for 142 years, we've been here building on a lot 
of trust that the consumers have bestowed on us during this time. It feels great 
to have the privilege and the honour to be part of this business. And now, to 
be able to look to take it forward as we speak. You're familiar with the fact that 
Dabur is in 8 out of 10 Indian households. We always keep talking about the 
distribution reach that Dabur has. But, you know, when I look at the portfolio, 
what really stood out for me at that moment was the sheer size and play across 
categories that we have. Be it home and personal care, be it healthcare, or be 
it F&B, and of course, our Ayurveda business, we've got strong brands that have 
played across the board. So right at the top, you have the 1,000 crore-plus 
brands. In the middle, you have those brands that have a lot of opportunity, 
but more importantly, they are robust category leaders, defining category, 
defining brands, with a lot of headroom, given that we still have low levels of 
penetration here. I think the exciting part is what you see at the bottom. These 
are the brands, the brands of the future. The brands that have a lot of potential. 
And anyone who gets the opportunity to get a stable of brands that looks like 
this should consider themselves as a leader, lucky to be at the helm of driving 
change or driving what comes next. Now, our aim, or ambition, is to be, or to 
play a leading role in the categories that we are part of. 

 
What you see on the page are the brands that hold strong market leadership, 
category-defining brands, and these brands are the core that contribute to over 
50% of our revenue. So, very clearly, when I was looking at this, I was seeing 
that this is an organisation with a huge heritage, a very rich legacy, and amazing 
brands. But most importantly, it had something for everyone across India. So 
that's how I saw Dabur from the outside as I came in: as an organisation that is 
playing across rural, across urban; it's playing across the mass segment; it's 
playing across premium. It has a portfolio that is built for every consumer, every 
market, every single channel, and can cater to every single occasion. 
 
 
That's the first part of how I saw things. Now, I got the privilege to spend the 
first 6 months doing a lot of listening, doing a lot of learning, and gaining a lot 
of understanding of what Dabur is. And some of the things that came up in my 
conversation with what I call the three C's, which are the most integral part of 
any organisation: our consumers, our customers, and our colleagues, were very 
rich in terms of insights. So when I met a consumer, the one key thing that kept 
coming across to me was the trust that we'd built with them, and our 
responsibility to ensure we hold on to that trust with everything and every step 
we take. With our customers, I met some of them who've been with us for over 
50 years. You know, this is not a normal relationship. This is a relationship 
where you become an integral part of one's family, and you grow together. And 
we've been blessed to have customers who've been with us over generations. 
And finally, we did these Unplugged with Herjit sessions that allowed me to 
spend over 100 hours with small groups of people within the organisation, 
across regions, across channels, where I asked them a very simple question: 
What's the one thing that you love about Dabur that you would like to retain? 
And what's the one thing that frustrates you and that you'd like to change? 
 
So, a lot of rich insights. A lot of things that we can feel really proud of, and I 
honestly feel that we don't get the level of credit that we have for the strong 
fundamentals that this organisation has.  
 
At the same time, there were very clear opportunity areas that came through. 
Right? One of the clear messages I heard from across the board was that we 
have great brands. We need to be focused, and we need to enhance our 
spending behind our brands. Are we spending enough? The other area that 
came through to me clearly in the messaging was that we are the house of 
Ayurveda. We need to be the leaders in health and wellness. And we should do 
more in this space. Then, of course, the other thing which also came through 
was: How do we transform our portfolio to meet the changing needs of the 
Indian consumer? So there's work that's happening, but how do we do it 
faster? And finally, it was in the area of excellence around our execution. We 
have a great execution; how do we enhance the quality of that execution? So 
those were the four things that I really picked up from all of the understanding, 
so that it goes into looking at how we write the future.  
 
 
Having said this, the 6 months that I've been part of the company have also 
been an incredible 6 months from a macro environment perspective. And I 
know each one of you knows this far better than I do. But the environment has 
been challenging, given the Middle East conflict, resulting in crude prices going 
up and higher inflation. But for us, within FMCG across the board, it's been a 
challenging environment in order to drive consumption. It's been an 

environment where inflation has been elevated, and we've had to calibrate 
what we are doing. My focus, and my team's focus during this time, is very 
simple: control the controllables. We can only influence that which is in our 
control. And in doing so, our approach has been to look at this as an 
opportunity, to look across the length and breadth of our portfolio, to be able 
to see how we can enhance our mix, how we can drive cost optimisation more, 
how we can take calibrated price increases, and where we need to be 
competitive. So all of that's been happening in this environment.  
 
But I think at the fundamental of it all, and what's probably most heartening, 
and like I said, you guys know this better than I do, is that India's growth story 
continues to remain as robust as it has been. We are the fastest-growing 
economy. We are having a much younger workforce that is also getting digitally 
savvier as we speak. There is a far higher need for health and wellness. 
Consumers are looking at labels with a very different perspective, as well as the 
whole opportunity across quick commerce. Now, the way I see this is: wow, this 
is exactly where Dabur needs to reinforce its position of strength from over the 
years and bring itself to make a bigger play here. We have the headroom for 
growth. Right? We have the credentials as far as natural and Ayurvedic equity 
exists, backed by science. We have the rural reach. We have the urban strength 
across the channels. So, when I looked at this, for me, coming into the 
organisation was an amazing opportunity to be part of the future of this 
amazing organisation, and help build it, in a way that I can contribute. 
 
 
 
So, from that on, I started to look at one of the ways that you look to build the 
future is to look at the past. And we started with doing an assessment of our 
vision. Now, some of you may know that we do a vision on a 3-year cycle. So 
we build a vision. Of course, given the world we live in, we can calibrate the 
vision on an annual basis, but we build the vision on a 3-year cycle. We are, as 
we speak, 18 months into that vision. And, for the first time and in a very 
unfiltered, real manner, I'm going to share with you an assessment of where I 
believe we are at the end of these 18 months, and what we need to do as we 
go into the next part of the vision. 
 
Now, what you see on the page are clearly the seven areas that we said we 
would focus on: the seven key pillars of our vision that were laid out 18 months 
ago. The first one was to accelerate our core brands. The second one was to 
make our brands more premium and contemporary. The third one was to take 
big, bold bets in the area of health and wellness. The fourth one was to simplify 
and streamline our portfolio. The fifth one was to enhance our go-to-market. 
The sixth one was to do strategic M&A, and the seventh one was to build 
operating efficiencies. So I'm going to now just dive in, give you a quick 
perspective of where I feel we are and how we did against that till now. 
 
 
 
So the first one, in terms of accelerating our core brands, these are our core; 
these are the brands that generate almost 60% of our business. They're all 
strong brands. Our focus during this time has to be to continue driving 
investment in these core brands so that we can enhance the category, because 
we are market leaders in many of them. We can further build relevance, and 
we can drive usage and occasions to grow penetration as we go along. Now, we 
recently released a new communication, and I'm going to share that with you 
on Chyawanprash. I know a lot of you are going to be interested and excited 

about what we are doing since we are getting into Chyawanprash season. One 
of our key focus areas with Chyawanprash has been to build relevance and 
drive more occasions. We are doing it through this new communication, as well 
as through newer formats in the form of gummies, but let's take a sneak peek 
at this new communication that just went live two days ago. 
[Advertisement playback: Chyawanprash campaign]  
 
Yeah, so that's something that went live two days ago. There's one more 
campaign that I want to talk to you about, which is around Odonil. It's one of 
our key brands, a core brand in the home care space, and one brand that we 
believe has a lot of potential in terms of growth and in terms of opportunity. 
For the first time, we came out with a campaign that goes across regions, and 
it talks to consumers in their language, in the region we are in. So, since today 
we are in Mumbai, for all the Mumbaikars, can we have the new Odonil 
campaign, please? 
 
[Advertisement playback: Odonil regional campaign] 
 
I think we've done good work in the space of accelerating our core brands, but 
we've had to calibrate investments, given the hyperinflation that we have seen, 
and I will talk a little more about it. But the other area that I believe we've done 
a good job in has been in the area of digital, where we've really accelerated our 
spending on digital; our media spend, as far as digital is concerned, now are 
almost 43% of our total spend. But what's really heartening to see is how the 
team has driven efficiency, and as a result of the efficiency, we've been able to 
really drive a lot more out of the campaigns that we've spent. All of you, I'm 
sure, have seen our results, and you've seen our Q2 media spend, but what has 
been important is how we've spent that money and where we've spent that 
money, which has been able to drive a lot more relevance for us, and more 
importantly, we've upped our influencers by over 3X, and we've been able to 
do it by driving a lot more efficiency. We're also using a complete 360 approach 
on our key brands.  
 
To be able to drive the right conversations, whether it's on the relevant digital 
screen, online, or with access to the right influencers. So I do want to share 
with you one communication that just went live, where we are talking about 
honey, and again, this is the season of honey, so about driving the purity of 
honey, and just taking you through how honey is made. So, can we just look at 
the honey campaign, please? 
 
[Advertisement playback: Dabur Honey] 
 
Yeah, and there's been a lot of use of AI now, especially in how we do our media 
planning. We're also using AI in terms of helping us generate content, right? So 
I just want to show you one communication that is made in-home, and that's 
also another way we are able to maximize our media output and make it more 
consumer-facing. So this is one classic example of how we are doing that. Can 
we see the next one? 
 
[Advertisement playback: Real Cranberry campaign] 
 
Now, when I look at this, you will see at the bottom, I've put a small grading 
scale. As far as I can see it, I have still rated this first pillar of ours in the amber. 
Why have I done it? I've done it because, while we've generated the growth on 
our core brands that we had put as part of the vision, we fell short on the media 
spending or the support that we had committed to put behind it. Of course, 
that was driven by the environment. However, it's something, it's a good 
assessment of where I see it right now, so that it allows us to build what the 
focus is going to be going forward. So that was the first pillar. 

 
 
 
Quickly onto the second pillar, which is around premiumization. Here, we have 
been really focused on how we can really service the needs of our consumers 
by evolving through their evolving needs, and through our higher-margin 
portfolio. Now, I'm very happy to share with you that, for us, our premium 
portfolio used to contribute 17%. It has now gone up during these 18 months 
from 17% to 20%, and this premium portfolio is growing at 4X our overall rate 
and is margin accretive. So, it's a very simple formula as far as I see it that we 
need to continue to grow and to advance premiumization for us, because it's 
going to be able to sustain a higher top line and a higher top line which is more 
profitable. And there have been some great examples of premiumization, 
whether it's on honey, where we've got our organic honey, we've got our 
region-specific honey, and now we're about to launch a monofloral honey later 
this month. And all of these operate at 2.5 times the cost of normal honey, so 
there is a lot of work that's happening on making honey more relevant, offering 
consumers different kinds of premium opportunities. Similarly, on toothpaste 
with charcoal, I just want to share one last ad with you, which talks about how 
we are driving this premiumization, so you get a real sense of what we are 
doing. 
 
[Advertisement playback: Activated charcoal toothpaste campaign] 
 
Yeah, and the second leg of driving premiumization was really making our 
portfolio look a lot more contemporary. Again, there's been good work with 
the launch of new products. We've launched our first bio-infusion shampoo, 
which is “no salt”, that's gone out. We've got our new Oxy DeTan face packs 
that we're getting a very good response from. There have been new formats, 
and there's been new packaging. And one of the areas that we've really been 
focused on is how we enhance the packaging of our portfolio to make it more 
contemporary and make it more modern. And you see that classic example 
being the new packaging for Dabur Red, amongst the others that we have here. 
 
On this one, I have rated us on the verge of getting into green, because I think 
there's great work, we've seen the results, and we now just need to sustain and 
make it happen a lot more. 
 
 
 
The next pillar, or the third pillar, was really on bold bets in health and wellness. 
In terms of the opportunity here, it was very clear. Gut health is something that 
we are focused on. Our digestive business, comprising Hajmola, Pudin Hara, 
and Isabgol, has done incredibly well for us. We've been growing at strong 
double-digit growth in this space. We need to keep up the momentum. There 
is opportunity to do more in the area of functional beverages, as well as 
strength and vitality, versus what we had laid out at the start of the 18 months. 
So here, I've given us another amber here, because I believe there is more 
headroom to grow. So right now, I'm being tough on ourselves because we are 
getting solid growth from this portfolio, but it's the opportunity that we can 
look at together if we were to put more focus on investments in this space. So, 
that's the rating there. 
 
 
 
The next one was around simplification. A lot of you would have heard that our 
portfolio is diverse. We play in multiple categories. And within multiple 
categories, we have multiple brands. So one of the areas that we've been 
focused on is to rationalise, to simplify, and to drive prioritisation in terms of 
what we focus on. So, 6 brands, 350 SKUs, are gone. I've given us a rating of 

green in this space, but I promise you this is going to be a big area of focus as 
we look to our future as well, because this is where we will be able to ensure 
that we focus our energies on the few big priorities that we are going to be 
focused on. 
 
 
 
Moving on, the next pillar, which was our fifth pillar, was on Project Saksham. 
Saksham was put together to be able to really recalibrate and evolve our go-to-
market to meet the changing retail landscape that we are seeing across the 
country. That was the focus. In the area of GT, general trade, most of the 
numbers you see here are general trade numbers. We've carried out a very 
massive consolidation exercise over the last year. It's resulted in a reduction in 
our distributors by about 43%. And honestly, it was the need of the hour, and 
I'm glad the teams have done such a strong job of it, because that has resulted 
in lower distributor attrition by almost 80%. It has resulted in their throughput 
going up by 2X. It has resulted in their ROI going up by 30%. So, very clearly, 
there's been strong work here, work that is already beginning to show results. 
We've now delivered two quarters where our growth on GT has been mid-
single digit growth. This quarter, we've delivered our highest growth in the last 
many quarters, I think 19 quarters or so, in GT. And that's beginning to come 
through from Saksham. Now, at this stage, I will not say Saksham is done and 
complete. There is a lot more to be done here. And we will talk about it as I go 
further in this presentation. But for the work that was laid out, we believe that 
we've done a good job, and hence, that's where I've rated us green on that one. 
 
 
 
The next one, the sixth one, and I'm sure all of you will be wanting to see how 
I rate this one. This was on strategic M&A. We clearly called out a priority, and 
we put a number behind what we were looking to get at this stage. We're 
looking at M&A in two parts. One is in the area of taking a minority stake in 
D2C companies, which allows us to learn, understand trends, and engage and 
play a role in how these companies evolve with the founders. We got RAS as 
part of Dabur Ventures. Dabur Ventures was formed on October 2025, and RAS 
was the first investment that was done earlier this year. So that's one aspect of 
it. And then, as far as strategic acquisitions go, and that's the big area that we 
had called out as part of this vision, we'd acquired Badshah, which continues 
to deliver robust growth. We've got Sesa that's going to be integrated starting 
1st of December into the Dabur business, and it is going to be integrated with 
retrospective effect from 1st April. However, in terms of looking at everything 
we had set out for ourselves to do, I've given us a red on this front. It's been 18 
months. We still have 18 months to go, so this red can become a green. But at 
this stage, this is where we stand. And at this stage, I do also want to 
acknowledge that we're not looking at doing an M&A for the sake of doing an 
M&A; we are looking at doing an M&A if it meets the strategic requirements of 
where Dabur is and where Dabur needs to get to. 
 
It meets the ability of us to be able to generate synergies, both from a 
distribution and a supply chain perspective. It meets the right “wagon wheel” 
within which we want to operate. And, most importantly, it comes at the right 
valuation, because that's going to be critical for us as we close this out. But 
right now, 18 months in, on this vision, this is where we are on this initiative. 
 
 
 
And the last one was around operating efficiencies. Now, the role of operating 
efficiencies as a pillar was to make us more efficient from a supply chain 

perspective, so how do we manage our costs, and how do we do better from 
that aspect of business, from a manufacturing or from a product portfolio 
perspective, and this is where our project Samriddhi, which is the cost-saving 
initiative that we drive within the organisation, has been working for us.  
We've generated over 115 crores during the vision period that has allowed us 
to be able to deliver what we've been delivering. Even on this front, I've given 
ourselves towards the green, because this was in line with the goals that we 
had set out at that time.  
 
 
 
So that, really, was the 7 key pillars of our vision. And I have honestly put a 
scorecard out there in front of you that tells you that there are some areas that 
we are doing really well. We will continue to keep doing well. There are some 
areas that are opportunities, and that's how I see them, because there is a 
quick difference that we could make in some of those areas, and some that we 
need to continue working on more from a future, long-term perspective. 
 
 
 
At this stage, I do want to tell you that we do a vision every 3 years. So ideally, 
the next vision exercise is only to happen in March of 2028. But with everything 
that one has been working on with the team, we believe that the time is right 
for us to get into a strategic midterm exercise that we will initiate now, right? 
So, I look forward to coming back to you all in the next 6 to 8 months with a 
medium-term vision that talks about a 2031 plan and sharing with you what 
things we will continue to keep doing. What are the things that we are going to 
accelerate in terms of how we evolve our portfolio and make it future-ready? 
And what are the things that we are going to be doing in terms of execution? 
So, look out for that. That's what we're going to be doing in the next 6 to 8 
months. 
 
Having said this, when we were spending time with people within the 
organisation, one of the key feelings we were picking up was: what do we do 
differently now? What are we going to do to step change? You've seen the step 
change in the last two months when you look at our performance, but it's early 
days. It's something that needs a lot more work to be done. So, how are we 
going to do that? And we were looking to put out a mantra that we want to 
bring to our lives and the organisation. 
 
 
Now, let me just remind you, this is not a new strategy; this is our mantra to 
reignite the organisation, and that's what is called as Ignite. You see Ignite 
everywhere. We believe that if we come together, we can fuel growth by 
winning together, and for that, we need to ignite the entire organisation of 
Dabur India to really, as I say, come to the party. And that is what we're going 
to be focused on going forward. Now, what exactly is going to happen in this 
area in the immediate future? We've already been working on Ignite for the 
last 3 months. We're focused on 4 key areas. 
 
 
 
We want to accelerate growth; that's very clear. That is something that this 
business needs to be doing, and has the right to do so. We want to further 
enhance our execution. We want to build a future-ready portfolio. And lastly, 
we need to find the money to invest behind all of this. So, very clearly, four key 
priorities. 
 
 

 
The first one is on accelerating the core. We call it energise the core and scale 
the stars. So, as part of Ignite, we are going to be energising the core. How are 
we going to do that? We believe we haven't put in as much investment in 
certain areas of our core. We're going to do that, and for that, we're going to 
look to invest 150 to 200 basis points of advertising and promotion extra, or 
media investments that go further in those areas. Now, this needs to be in the 
area of consumer-facing investments on brands where we feel we are going to 
get the biggest return on that investment. 
 
 
 
Then it's going to be scaling our stars. We have amazing stars that I spoke to 
you about. There is opportunity in some of these, and we will look to ensure 
that, especially in certain areas, we invest disproportionately, in the area of 
OTCs and digestives, in some parts of our skincare, home care, and foods 
portfolio, that allows us to continue growing at strong double-digit in the stars 
part of our portfolio. With this, we are reiterating our guidance for the full year 
to remain at double-digit. We'd call that out at the start of the year. We've 
managed to deliver that a little ahead of that, in the first two quarters, and we 
look to maintain that momentum going forward for the remainder of the year 
as well. So that's the first one. 
 
 
 
On the second one, in the area of execution excellence, a lot gets spoken about 
Dabur's reach, the quantity of coverage. A lot of numbers get spoken about. I 
want to tweak this with my team to focus now on the quality of coverage. It's 
not just reach that's important; it is what we are getting out of that reach that's 
going to be important. And in order to do so, we are ramping up our channel 
program. And that is something that we're now building across 40,000 stores. 
We call it the Retail Next program. Within that, we are very clear that we want 
to deliver growth that is 1.5 times the growth of the rest of GT, and we're going 
to be doing that with very clear ways of working, ways of selling in, the use of 
MSL in terms of what is the right portfolio, what quantity needs to be sold, and 
what is the right level of visibility that we want inside these stores. So, this is 
going to be a big focus. The aim is to drive pull for our brands with a 
combination of enhancing our media on-air, driving more digital, and ensuring 
that they are visible and available in the high-weighted stores that we focus on.

MANAGEMENT: 
MR. HERJIT BHALLA – CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER – INDIA BUSINESS – 
DABUR INDIA LIMITED 
MR. ANKUSH JAIN – CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER – DABUR INDIA LIMITED 
MR. RAHUL SARAWAGI – HEAD, INVESTOR RELATIONS AND M&A – 
DABUR INDIA LIMITED 
 

 
Rahul Sarawagi: 
Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. A very warm welcome to all of you and 
thank you very much for coming to this event and taking the time to join us in 
person. It's a pleasure to have with us our valued investors, analysts, as well as 
members from the financial fraternity. Your continued engagement with Dabur, 
your perspectives and your valuable feedback are always welcome and 
appreciated. Dabur is a company with a rich heritage and a distinctive place in 
India's consumer landscape. Over the years, we have built a business around a 
deep understanding of consumers, a strong connection with our brands, and a 
continued focus on health, wellness, and everyday household needs. 
I'm sure you must have already gone through our Q2 FY27 results. But today, 
this goes a step further. Here, we'll be talking more about what our perspective 
is on our business; what the key focus areas are; how we have progressed; and 
what opportunities lie ahead. Today, over the course of today's session, Mr 
Herjit Bhalla, who is our India Business CEO, will take us through the 
presentation, which will be followed by a Q&A session. With that, I would now 
like to invite Herjit to come on stage and take us through the presentation. 
 
 
Herjit Bhalla: 
Thank you, Rahul. A very good afternoon to all of you. Thank you for being here, 
and in advance, wishing all of you the best for Diwali. So, I'm Herjit Bhalla, and 
I am delighted to be here today to have this conversation with you, to share 
with you how I have seen the last 6 months go, and also to take some insights 
from you on what you guys are thinking as well. So the agenda for the next little 
bit is going to be as follows. We're just going to do a very quick look at Dabur 
as I saw it when I was coming into the organisation, and what I believe I have 
learned in my first 6 months. I'm also going to do a quick assessment of our 
performance and what we're going to be doing next. 
 
 
So, very clearly, you know, it's rare that you join a new organisation and you've 
already been familiar with and using the brands for many decades. That's how 
day one at Dabur felt, right? This is truly an amazing organisation with a very 
rich heritage. We're all aware: for 142 years, we've been here building on a lot 
of trust that the consumers have bestowed on us during this time. It feels great 
to have the privilege and the honour to be part of this business. And now, to 
be able to look to take it forward as we speak. You're familiar with the fact that 
Dabur is in 8 out of 10 Indian households. We always keep talking about the 
distribution reach that Dabur has. But, you know, when I look at the portfolio, 
what really stood out for me at that moment was the sheer size and play across 
categories that we have. Be it home and personal care, be it healthcare, or be 
it F&B, and of course, our Ayurveda business, we've got strong brands that have 
played across the board. So right at the top, you have the 1,000 crore-plus 
brands. In the middle, you have those brands that have a lot of opportunity, 
but more importantly, they are robust category leaders, defining category, 
defining brands, with a lot of headroom, given that we still have low levels of 
penetration here. I think the exciting part is what you see at the bottom. These 
are the brands, the brands of the future. The brands that have a lot of potential. 
And anyone who gets the opportunity to get a stable of brands that looks like 
this should consider themselves as a leader, lucky to be at the helm of driving 
change or driving what comes next. Now, our aim, or ambition, is to be, or to 
play a leading role in the categories that we are part of. 

 
What you see on the page are the brands that hold strong market leadership, 
category-defining brands, and these brands are the core that contribute to over 
50% of our revenue. So, very clearly, when I was looking at this, I was seeing 
that this is an organisation with a huge heritage, a very rich legacy, and amazing 
brands. But most importantly, it had something for everyone across India. So 
that's how I saw Dabur from the outside as I came in: as an organisation that is 
playing across rural, across urban; it's playing across the mass segment; it's 
playing across premium. It has a portfolio that is built for every consumer, every 
market, every single channel, and can cater to every single occasion. 
 
 
That's the first part of how I saw things. Now, I got the privilege to spend the 
first 6 months doing a lot of listening, doing a lot of learning, and gaining a lot 
of understanding of what Dabur is. And some of the things that came up in my 
conversation with what I call the three C's, which are the most integral part of 
any organisation: our consumers, our customers, and our colleagues, were very 
rich in terms of insights. So when I met a consumer, the one key thing that kept 
coming across to me was the trust that we'd built with them, and our 
responsibility to ensure we hold on to that trust with everything and every step 
we take. With our customers, I met some of them who've been with us for over 
50 years. You know, this is not a normal relationship. This is a relationship 
where you become an integral part of one's family, and you grow together. And 
we've been blessed to have customers who've been with us over generations. 
And finally, we did these Unplugged with Herjit sessions that allowed me to 
spend over 100 hours with small groups of people within the organisation, 
across regions, across channels, where I asked them a very simple question: 
What's the one thing that you love about Dabur that you would like to retain? 
And what's the one thing that frustrates you and that you'd like to change? 
 
So, a lot of rich insights. A lot of things that we can feel really proud of, and I 
honestly feel that we don't get the level of credit that we have for the strong 
fundamentals that this organisation has.  
 
At the same time, there were very clear opportunity areas that came through. 
Right? One of the clear messages I heard from across the board was that we 
have great brands. We need to be focused, and we need to enhance our 
spending behind our brands. Are we spending enough? The other area that 
came through to me clearly in the messaging was that we are the house of 
Ayurveda. We need to be the leaders in health and wellness. And we should do 
more in this space. Then, of course, the other thing which also came through 
was: How do we transform our portfolio to meet the changing needs of the 
Indian consumer? So there's work that's happening, but how do we do it 
faster? And finally, it was in the area of excellence around our execution. We 
have a great execution; how do we enhance the quality of that execution? So 
those were the four things that I really picked up from all of the understanding, 
so that it goes into looking at how we write the future.  
 
 
Having said this, the 6 months that I've been part of the company have also 
been an incredible 6 months from a macro environment perspective. And I 
know each one of you knows this far better than I do. But the environment has 
been challenging, given the Middle East conflict, resulting in crude prices going 
up and higher inflation. But for us, within FMCG across the board, it's been a 
challenging environment in order to drive consumption. It's been an 

environment where inflation has been elevated, and we've had to calibrate 
what we are doing. My focus, and my team's focus during this time, is very 
simple: control the controllables. We can only influence that which is in our 
control. And in doing so, our approach has been to look at this as an 
opportunity, to look across the length and breadth of our portfolio, to be able 
to see how we can enhance our mix, how we can drive cost optimisation more, 
how we can take calibrated price increases, and where we need to be 
competitive. So all of that's been happening in this environment.  
 
But I think at the fundamental of it all, and what's probably most heartening, 
and like I said, you guys know this better than I do, is that India's growth story 
continues to remain as robust as it has been. We are the fastest-growing 
economy. We are having a much younger workforce that is also getting digitally 
savvier as we speak. There is a far higher need for health and wellness. 
Consumers are looking at labels with a very different perspective, as well as the 
whole opportunity across quick commerce. Now, the way I see this is: wow, this 
is exactly where Dabur needs to reinforce its position of strength from over the 
years and bring itself to make a bigger play here. We have the headroom for 
growth. Right? We have the credentials as far as natural and Ayurvedic equity 
exists, backed by science. We have the rural reach. We have the urban strength 
across the channels. So, when I looked at this, for me, coming into the 
organisation was an amazing opportunity to be part of the future of this 
amazing organisation, and help build it, in a way that I can contribute. 
 
 
 
So, from that on, I started to look at one of the ways that you look to build the 
future is to look at the past. And we started with doing an assessment of our 
vision. Now, some of you may know that we do a vision on a 3-year cycle. So 
we build a vision. Of course, given the world we live in, we can calibrate the 
vision on an annual basis, but we build the vision on a 3-year cycle. We are, as 
we speak, 18 months into that vision. And, for the first time and in a very 
unfiltered, real manner, I'm going to share with you an assessment of where I 
believe we are at the end of these 18 months, and what we need to do as we 
go into the next part of the vision. 
 
Now, what you see on the page are clearly the seven areas that we said we 
would focus on: the seven key pillars of our vision that were laid out 18 months 
ago. The first one was to accelerate our core brands. The second one was to 
make our brands more premium and contemporary. The third one was to take 
big, bold bets in the area of health and wellness. The fourth one was to simplify 
and streamline our portfolio. The fifth one was to enhance our go-to-market. 
The sixth one was to do strategic M&A, and the seventh one was to build 
operating efficiencies. So I'm going to now just dive in, give you a quick 
perspective of where I feel we are and how we did against that till now. 
 
 
 
So the first one, in terms of accelerating our core brands, these are our core; 
these are the brands that generate almost 60% of our business. They're all 
strong brands. Our focus during this time has to be to continue driving 
investment in these core brands so that we can enhance the category, because 
we are market leaders in many of them. We can further build relevance, and 
we can drive usage and occasions to grow penetration as we go along. Now, we 
recently released a new communication, and I'm going to share that with you 
on Chyawanprash. I know a lot of you are going to be interested and excited 

about what we are doing since we are getting into Chyawanprash season. One 
of our key focus areas with Chyawanprash has been to build relevance and 
drive more occasions. We are doing it through this new communication, as well 
as through newer formats in the form of gummies, but let's take a sneak peek 
at this new communication that just went live two days ago. 
[Advertisement playback: Chyawanprash campaign]  
 
Yeah, so that's something that went live two days ago. There's one more 
campaign that I want to talk to you about, which is around Odonil. It's one of 
our key brands, a core brand in the home care space, and one brand that we 
believe has a lot of potential in terms of growth and in terms of opportunity. 
For the first time, we came out with a campaign that goes across regions, and 
it talks to consumers in their language, in the region we are in. So, since today 
we are in Mumbai, for all the Mumbaikars, can we have the new Odonil 
campaign, please? 
 
[Advertisement playback: Odonil regional campaign] 
 
I think we've done good work in the space of accelerating our core brands, but 
we've had to calibrate investments, given the hyperinflation that we have seen, 
and I will talk a little more about it. But the other area that I believe we've done 
a good job in has been in the area of digital, where we've really accelerated our 
spending on digital; our media spend, as far as digital is concerned, now are 
almost 43% of our total spend. But what's really heartening to see is how the 
team has driven efficiency, and as a result of the efficiency, we've been able to 
really drive a lot more out of the campaigns that we've spent. All of you, I'm 
sure, have seen our results, and you've seen our Q2 media spend, but what has 
been important is how we've spent that money and where we've spent that 
money, which has been able to drive a lot more relevance for us, and more 
importantly, we've upped our influencers by over 3X, and we've been able to 
do it by driving a lot more efficiency. We're also using a complete 360 approach 
on our key brands.  
 
To be able to drive the right conversations, whether it's on the relevant digital 
screen, online, or with access to the right influencers. So I do want to share 
with you one communication that just went live, where we are talking about 
honey, and again, this is the season of honey, so about driving the purity of 
honey, and just taking you through how honey is made. So, can we just look at 
the honey campaign, please? 
 
[Advertisement playback: Dabur Honey] 
 
Yeah, and there's been a lot of use of AI now, especially in how we do our media 
planning. We're also using AI in terms of helping us generate content, right? So 
I just want to show you one communication that is made in-home, and that's 
also another way we are able to maximize our media output and make it more 
consumer-facing. So this is one classic example of how we are doing that. Can 
we see the next one? 
 
[Advertisement playback: Real Cranberry campaign] 
 
Now, when I look at this, you will see at the bottom, I've put a small grading 
scale. As far as I can see it, I have still rated this first pillar of ours in the amber. 
Why have I done it? I've done it because, while we've generated the growth on 
our core brands that we had put as part of the vision, we fell short on the media 
spending or the support that we had committed to put behind it. Of course, 
that was driven by the environment. However, it's something, it's a good 
assessment of where I see it right now, so that it allows us to build what the 
focus is going to be going forward. So that was the first pillar. 

 
 
 
Quickly onto the second pillar, which is around premiumization. Here, we have 
been really focused on how we can really service the needs of our consumers 
by evolving through their evolving needs, and through our higher-margin 
portfolio. Now, I'm very happy to share with you that, for us, our premium 
portfolio used to contribute 17%. It has now gone up during these 18 months 
from 17% to 20%, and this premium portfolio is growing at 4X our overall rate 
and is margin accretive. So, it's a very simple formula as far as I see it that we 
need to continue to grow and to advance premiumization for us, because it's 
going to be able to sustain a higher top line and a higher top line which is more 
profitable. And there have been some great examples of premiumization, 
whether it's on honey, where we've got our organic honey, we've got our 
region-specific honey, and now we're about to launch a monofloral honey later 
this month. And all of these operate at 2.5 times the cost of normal honey, so 
there is a lot of work that's happening on making honey more relevant, offering 
consumers different kinds of premium opportunities. Similarly, on toothpaste 
with charcoal, I just want to share one last ad with you, which talks about how 
we are driving this premiumization, so you get a real sense of what we are 
doing. 
 
[Advertisement playback: Activated charcoal toothpaste campaign] 
 
Yeah, and the second leg of driving premiumization was really making our 
portfolio look a lot more contemporary. Again, there's been good work with 
the launch of new products. We've launched our first bio-infusion shampoo, 
which is “no salt”, that's gone out. We've got our new Oxy DeTan face packs 
that we're getting a very good response from. There have been new formats, 
and there's been new packaging. And one of the areas that we've really been 
focused on is how we enhance the packaging of our portfolio to make it more 
contemporary and make it more modern. And you see that classic example 
being the new packaging for Dabur Red, amongst the others that we have here. 
 
On this one, I have rated us on the verge of getting into green, because I think 
there's great work, we've seen the results, and we now just need to sustain and 
make it happen a lot more. 
 
 
 
The next pillar, or the third pillar, was really on bold bets in health and wellness. 
In terms of the opportunity here, it was very clear. Gut health is something that 
we are focused on. Our digestive business, comprising Hajmola, Pudin Hara, 
and Isabgol, has done incredibly well for us. We've been growing at strong 
double-digit growth in this space. We need to keep up the momentum. There 
is opportunity to do more in the area of functional beverages, as well as 
strength and vitality, versus what we had laid out at the start of the 18 months. 
So here, I've given us another amber here, because I believe there is more 
headroom to grow. So right now, I'm being tough on ourselves because we are 
getting solid growth from this portfolio, but it's the opportunity that we can 
look at together if we were to put more focus on investments in this space. So, 
that's the rating there. 
 
 
 
The next one was around simplification. A lot of you would have heard that our 
portfolio is diverse. We play in multiple categories. And within multiple 
categories, we have multiple brands. So one of the areas that we've been 
focused on is to rationalise, to simplify, and to drive prioritisation in terms of 
what we focus on. So, 6 brands, 350 SKUs, are gone. I've given us a rating of 

green in this space, but I promise you this is going to be a big area of focus as 
we look to our future as well, because this is where we will be able to ensure 
that we focus our energies on the few big priorities that we are going to be 
focused on. 
 
 
 
Moving on, the next pillar, which was our fifth pillar, was on Project Saksham. 
Saksham was put together to be able to really recalibrate and evolve our go-to-
market to meet the changing retail landscape that we are seeing across the 
country. That was the focus. In the area of GT, general trade, most of the 
numbers you see here are general trade numbers. We've carried out a very 
massive consolidation exercise over the last year. It's resulted in a reduction in 
our distributors by about 43%. And honestly, it was the need of the hour, and 
I'm glad the teams have done such a strong job of it, because that has resulted 
in lower distributor attrition by almost 80%. It has resulted in their throughput 
going up by 2X. It has resulted in their ROI going up by 30%. So, very clearly, 
there's been strong work here, work that is already beginning to show results. 
We've now delivered two quarters where our growth on GT has been mid-
single digit growth. This quarter, we've delivered our highest growth in the last 
many quarters, I think 19 quarters or so, in GT. And that's beginning to come 
through from Saksham. Now, at this stage, I will not say Saksham is done and 
complete. There is a lot more to be done here. And we will talk about it as I go 
further in this presentation. But for the work that was laid out, we believe that 
we've done a good job, and hence, that's where I've rated us green on that one. 
 
 
 
The next one, the sixth one, and I'm sure all of you will be wanting to see how 
I rate this one. This was on strategic M&A. We clearly called out a priority, and 
we put a number behind what we were looking to get at this stage. We're 
looking at M&A in two parts. One is in the area of taking a minority stake in 
D2C companies, which allows us to learn, understand trends, and engage and 
play a role in how these companies evolve with the founders. We got RAS as 
part of Dabur Ventures. Dabur Ventures was formed on October 2025, and RAS 
was the first investment that was done earlier this year. So that's one aspect of 
it. And then, as far as strategic acquisitions go, and that's the big area that we 
had called out as part of this vision, we'd acquired Badshah, which continues 
to deliver robust growth. We've got Sesa that's going to be integrated starting 
1st of December into the Dabur business, and it is going to be integrated with 
retrospective effect from 1st April. However, in terms of looking at everything 
we had set out for ourselves to do, I've given us a red on this front. It's been 18 
months. We still have 18 months to go, so this red can become a green. But at 
this stage, this is where we stand. And at this stage, I do also want to 
acknowledge that we're not looking at doing an M&A for the sake of doing an 
M&A; we are looking at doing an M&A if it meets the strategic requirements of 
where Dabur is and where Dabur needs to get to. 
 
It meets the ability of us to be able to generate synergies, both from a 
distribution and a supply chain perspective. It meets the right “wagon wheel” 
within which we want to operate. And, most importantly, it comes at the right 
valuation, because that's going to be critical for us as we close this out. But 
right now, 18 months in, on this vision, this is where we are on this initiative. 
 
 
 
And the last one was around operating efficiencies. Now, the role of operating 
efficiencies as a pillar was to make us more efficient from a supply chain 

perspective, so how do we manage our costs, and how do we do better from 
that aspect of business, from a manufacturing or from a product portfolio 
perspective, and this is where our project Samriddhi, which is the cost-saving 
initiative that we drive within the organisation, has been working for us.  
We've generated over 115 crores during the vision period that has allowed us 
to be able to deliver what we've been delivering. Even on this front, I've given 
ourselves towards the green, because this was in line with the goals that we 
had set out at that time.  
 
 
 
So that, really, was the 7 key pillars of our vision. And I have honestly put a 
scorecard out there in front of you that tells you that there are some areas that 
we are doing really well. We will continue to keep doing well. There are some 
areas that are opportunities, and that's how I see them, because there is a 
quick difference that we could make in some of those areas, and some that we 
need to continue working on more from a future, long-term perspective. 
 
 
 
At this stage, I do want to tell you that we do a vision every 3 years. So ideally, 
the next vision exercise is only to happen in March of 2028. But with everything 
that one has been working on with the team, we believe that the time is right 
for us to get into a strategic midterm exercise that we will initiate now, right? 
So, I look forward to coming back to you all in the next 6 to 8 months with a 
medium-term vision that talks about a 2031 plan and sharing with you what 
things we will continue to keep doing. What are the things that we are going to 
accelerate in terms of how we evolve our portfolio and make it future-ready? 
And what are the things that we are going to be doing in terms of execution? 
So, look out for that. That's what we're going to be doing in the next 6 to 8 
months. 
 
Having said this, when we were spending time with people within the 
organisation, one of the key feelings we were picking up was: what do we do 
differently now? What are we going to do to step change? You've seen the step 
change in the last two months when you look at our performance, but it's early 
days. It's something that needs a lot more work to be done. So, how are we 
going to do that? And we were looking to put out a mantra that we want to 
bring to our lives and the organisation. 
 
 
Now, let me just remind you, this is not a new strategy; this is our mantra to 
reignite the organisation, and that's what is called as Ignite. You see Ignite 
everywhere. We believe that if we come together, we can fuel growth by 
winning together, and for that, we need to ignite the entire organisation of 
Dabur India to really, as I say, come to the party. And that is what we're going 
to be focused on going forward. Now, what exactly is going to happen in this 
area in the immediate future? We've already been working on Ignite for the 
last 3 months. We're focused on 4 key areas. 
 
 
 
We want to accelerate growth; that's very clear. That is something that this 
business needs to be doing, and has the right to do so. We want to further 
enhance our execution. We want to build a future-ready portfolio. And lastly, 
we need to find the money to invest behind all of this. So, very clearly, four key 
priorities. 
 
 

 
The first one is on accelerating the core. We call it energise the core and scale 
the stars. So, as part of Ignite, we are going to be energising the core. How are 
we going to do that? We believe we haven't put in as much investment in 
certain areas of our core. We're going to do that, and for that, we're going to 
look to invest 150 to 200 basis points of advertising and promotion extra, or 
media investments that go further in those areas. Now, this needs to be in the 
area of consumer-facing investments on brands where we feel we are going to 
get the biggest return on that investment. 
 
 
 
Then it's going to be scaling our stars. We have amazing stars that I spoke to 
you about. There is opportunity in some of these, and we will look to ensure 
that, especially in certain areas, we invest disproportionately, in the area of 
OTCs and digestives, in some parts of our skincare, home care, and foods 
portfolio, that allows us to continue growing at strong double-digit in the stars 
part of our portfolio. With this, we are reiterating our guidance for the full year 
to remain at double-digit. We'd call that out at the start of the year. We've 
managed to deliver that a little ahead of that, in the first two quarters, and we 
look to maintain that momentum going forward for the remainder of the year 
as well. So that's the first one. 
 
 
 
On the second one, in the area of execution excellence, a lot gets spoken about 
Dabur's reach, the quantity of coverage. A lot of numbers get spoken about. I

going to be important. And in order to do so, we are ramping up our channel 
program. And that is something that we're now building across 40,000 stores. 
We call it the Retail Next program. Within that, we are very clear that we want 
to deliver growth that is 1.5 times the growth of the rest of GT, and we're going 
to be doing that with very clear ways of working, ways of selling in, the use of

Press Release 
 
1 | P a g e 
 
 
Jindal Stainless wins 95 Gold and 6 Silver Awards at QCFI Conventions 2026 
 
• 
Jindal Stainless’ Hisar and Jajpur units were recognised at Chapter Conventions on Quality 
Concepts (CCQC) 2026 for quality initiatives, employee involvement and continuous improvement 
 
Jajpur/ Hisar, November 10, 2026: Jindal Stainless, India’s leading stainless steel manufacturer, has won 
95 Gold and 6 Silver Awards across the Quality Circle Forum of India (QCFI) conventions held in Delhi and 
Bhubaneswar, recognising the quality improvement initiatives and problem-solving efforts of its 
employees. 
 
The Jajpur unit won 71 Gold Awards at the 8th CCQC Bhubaneswar Chapter Convention 2026, along with 
earning the Highest Participation Award for fielding 71 teams, and receiving the prestigious Gyanadhara 
Award. On the other hand, the Hisar unit secured 24 Gold and 6 Silver Awards at the 41st CCQC Delhi 
Chapter Convention 2026. The awards recognised the efforts of its teams in identifying opportunities for 
improvement, addressing operational challenges and strengthening process efficiency. 
 
 
 

                                                                                 
Press Release 
 
2 | P a g e 
 
 
 
Congratulating the teams on the achievement, Unit Head – Jajpur, Jindal Stainless, Deepak Agrawal, 
said, “I am proud that Jindal Stainless’ representation with 71 teams was the first time the event saw such 
enthusiasm from a single company. The fact that all our teams received Gold Awards reflects the strong 
culture nurtured by our employees and their collective efforts in applying quality concepts and working 
towards better processes. I congratulate all the participants for their dedication, teamwork and problem-
solving approach.” 
 
Commenting on the agility and participation of the employees, Unit Head – Hisar, Jindal Stainless, Mr 
Vijay Bindlish, said, “The impressive performance of our Quality Circle teams reflects the proactive 
approach of our employees towards identifying opportunities for improvement and making meaningful 
contributions to the organisation. We have consistently encouraged our people to take ownership of 
processes, challenge existing practices and bring forward ideas that enhance quality and efficiency. Such 
platforms provide an excellent opportunity to recognise these efforts and inspire more employees to be 
part of our continuous improvement journey.” 
 
Participation in these conventions underscores Jindal Stainless’ sustained efforts to nurture a culture 
where employees actively contribute to improving processes, enhancing operational efficiency and 
driving innovation. The CCQC platform provides employees with an opportunity to showcase their 
problem solving initiatives, exchange knowledge and best practices with industry peers, and learn from 
experiences across organisations. It also fosters healthy competition, collaboration and employee-led 
improvement initiatives. 
 
 
About Jindal Stainless 

                                                                                 
Press Release 
 
3 | P a g e 
 
India’s leading stainless steel manufacturer, Jindal Stainless, had an annual turnover of INR 42,955 crore (USD 4.86 
billion) in FY26 and an annual melt capacity of 4.2 million tonnes. It has 16 stainless steel manufacturing and 
processing facilities in India and abroad, including in Spain and Indonesia, and a worldwide network in 12 countries, 
as of March 2026. In India, there are ten sales offices and six service centres, as of March 2026. The company’s 
product range includes stainless steel slabs, blooms, coils, plates, sheets, precision strips, wire rods, rebars, blade 
steel, and coin blanks. 
 
Jindal Stainless relies on its integrated operations to enhance its cost competitiveness and operational efficiency. 
Founded in 1970, Jindal Stainless continues to be inspired by a vision for innovation and enriching lives and is 
committed to social responsibility. 
 
Jindal Stainless remains focused on a greener and sustainable future. The company manufactures stainless steel 
using electric arc furnace, a process that significantly reduces greenhouse gas emissions and allows for recyclability 
of scrap without compromising on quality.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Exide Industries Limited Q2 FY27 Earning 
Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there 
will be an opportunity for you to ask a question. Should you need assistance during the 
conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then zero on your touchtone 
telephone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Raghunandhan from Nuvama Wealth Management. 
Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Raghu. 
Raghunandhan: 
Thank you, Sid. Good afternoon and Happy Diwali to everyone. From Exide Industries, we have 
with us MD and CEO, Mr. Avik Roy; Director Finance and CFO, Mr. Manoj Kumar Agarwal; 
President Legal and Corporate Affairs and Company Secretary, Mr. Jitendra Kumar, and Head 
of Investor Relations, Mr. Prashant Saraswat. Before we proceed, here is a disclaimer for the 
call. Few statements by the company's management in the call may be forward-looking in nature, 
and we request you to refer to the disclaimer in the earnings presentation for further details. 
 
We will start the call with brief opening remarks from the management, followed by Q&A 
sessions. I would like to congratulate the entire management team for robust results, and 
especially Mr. Avik Roy and Mr. Pravin Saraf for commissioning of 6 GWh lithium cell giga 
factory at Bengaluru. I now invite Mr. Avik Roy for opening remarks. Over to you, sir. 
Avik Roy: 
Thank you, Raghu. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and a warm welcome to you all to 
the Exide's quarter two earnings call. Just to add, our MD and CEO, Pravin Saraf, for the 
Lithium-Ion Project is also on call, in addition to the participants mentioned before. Today, I 
will cover how the market shaped up in quarter two, our business performance in quarter two, 
and the commissioning of our lithium-ion cell plant at Bengaluru, before closing with the near 
and mid-term market outlook. 
 
Overall, the demand held up well across our addressable markets during the quarter two. The 
affordability gains from GST rationalization supported the automotive demand, aided by healthy 
replacement market. Festive season buying has started, creating further demand since the end of 
the quarter. Vehicle registrations data of Vahan bears this out. Registrations rose by 1.3 million 
year-on-year for two-wheelers, which is an increase of 32%, and 0.3 million year-on-year for 
passenger vehicles, which is an increase of 27% year-on-year in quarter two. Partly on a soft 
base, last year's quarter two was pretty low, as buyers held back last year September purchases 
ahead of GST 2.0 implementation. Electric two-wheelers reached 11.6% of the two-wheeler 
retail in September, which is directly relevant for our lithium-ion business. 
 
We expect that two to three years from now, this automotive OEM demand will translate into 
aftermarket demand, for which we are getting prepared. Some of the new capacity expansions 
announcements by major OEMs are also encouraging us in this direction. Solar and infra push 
by the government is likely to drive our solar and stationary storage business in a big way. Now 
turning to company's performance. 
 
Standalone revenue for quarter two was INR5,026 crores, which is up 20.3% year-on-year. The 
growth momentum of quarter one carried into quarter two, taking our half-yearly revenue to 

 
 
Exide Industries Limited 
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 19 
 
INR10,331 crores, up by 18.9% year-on-year. This is the first time we have crossed INR10,000 
crores revenue milestone in half year. Input costs remained elevated vs last year due to prolonged 
geopolitical challenges, especially across West Asia, as well as a weaker rupee. 
 
Crude oil prices went up significantly, resulting in an overall inflationary environment. On a 
sequential quarter basis, the full benefits of softer lead or softer LME for lead and antimony 
prices could not be fully realized due to continuous weakening of rupee against the U.S. dollar. 
The company undertook various cost optimization initiatives to absorb this cost pressure. Further 
calibrated price increases and volume-led growth enabled the EBITDA margin expansion on a 
year-on-year basis. 
 
EBITDA came in at INR606 crores, up 53.6% year-on-year, and EBITDA margin improved to 
12.1% from 9.4% in the quarter two, resulting in an expansion of about 270 basis points on a 
low base. Last year's base of quarter two was pretty low for us. That also helped us. As you 
know, last year's quarter two was extraordinarily impacted by the sudden pre-GST 2.0-led 
demand slowdown, where we had to ramp down production to improve capital efficiency, and 
that had led to certain under absorption in our operations. 
 
For half year, EBITDA margin was 12.2%, up 130 basis points year-on-year. Half year pre-tax 
profits grew by 46.5% year-on-year. The balance sheet remains strong. We continue to be debt-
free and generate healthy operating cash flows. Let me take you through a bit deeper in the 
business insights for the quarter two of 2027. 
 
The automotive OEM business grew by over 25% for the fourth consecutive quarter, as vehicle 
makers stepped up production and dispatches. We gained high share across key upcoming OEM 
launches, the new launches, for example, MG Hector Tomahawk, and Tata Aeris. 
 
The two-wheeler and four-wheeler replacement business delivered its fourth consecutive quarter 
of double-digit growth, helped by a steadily expanding vehicle parc and the reach of our 
distribution network. Home inverters grew by 20% year-on-year, while solar grew by 40%+, 
supported by the favourable seasonal demand as well as the government initiatives, including 
the PM Surya Ghar Yojana. Exports grew by over 20% year-on-year for the second consecutive 
quarter on a low base. 
 
We have informed you in the past that last year, the exports business went through a deep decline 
because of global issues, and that is why on a low base, we have delivered 20% growth for the 
second consecutive quarter. This reflects our sustained efforts on geographic expansion and new 
product introductions. In September, we signed a long-term strategic cooperation agreement 
with the ExCom Energy Solutions GmbH, Germany. This is to expand our industrial battery and 
energy storage business across the European Economic Area. 
Industrial infrastructure, excluding telecom, grew by a high- single digit, supported by the 
industrial UPS as well as the traction motive power business. However, government tenders, 
mainly railways and power sector segment, continued to remain muted during the quarter. 

 
 
Exide Industries Limited 
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 19 
 
 
I would also like to touch upon the progress made through our ‘One Exide' operating model, 
which we have been communicating to the market for the last couple of years. This is an effort 
to bring the full strength of the organization together. We are increasingly sharing assets across 
businesses, combining our lead-acid market reach with emerging lithium-ion capabilities, and 
building a common digital engine across key functions. 
 
These actions have already unlocked substantial amount of additional four-wheeler battery 
capacity through which we are able to meet both the OEM as well as the aftermarket demand 
concurrently. This has accelerated the scale-up of our go-to-market of our lithium-ion last-mile 
solutions and improved productivity across the organization. Together, these initiatives are 
helping us to operate as one integrated company with a sharper customer focus, greater market 
outreach, and of course, last but not the least, much more efficient use of capital. 
 
Let me share an update on Exide Energy Solutions, our wholly owned subsidiary for lithium-
ion cells. 23rd September was a milestone for us. Exide Energy completed commissioning of 6 
GWh of lithium-ion cell plant in Bengaluru. In coming quarters, our focus is on stabilizing the 
lines and lifting the yields and ramping up the revenue. Customer qualification is progressing.  
 
We expect approvals from a few OEMs and telecom players in the near term. With E2-wheelers 
now close to 12% of the two-wheeler retail, this opportunity is growing. As of today, Exide's 
cumulative equity investment in EESL stands at INR5,352 crores, including INR550 crores 
invested in the current financial year. With this, I close my opening remarks. Over to you, 
Raghunandhan. We can now proceed with the Q&A.

the line of Raghunandhan from Nuvama Wealth Management. Please go ahead. 
Raghunandhan: 
Congratulations again, sir. Thank you for the detailed opening remarks presentation and also 
thanking the support of investor relations team. My first question is on the lithium business to 
Mr. Avik Roy and Mr. Pravin Saraf. On the lithium cell line, can you indicate how has been the 
response from customers on the cell sample acceptance? What is the progress for auto wins in 
both NMC and LFP lines? Can you highlight opportunities in auto, BESS, telecom, and other 
segments over the next two, three years? 
Avik Roy: 
I will take the first part of the question, Raghunandhan, and then I will request Pravin to take 
over on the outlook. As we mentioned in the previous quarters that we have been giving customer 
samples for their validation. As we speak, for some of the leading two-wheeler OEMs, the 
performance testing is over. Now they are doing the lifecycle testing. There is a process, there 
is a sequence. 
 
Lifecycle testing takes time, and once lifecycle testing is over, they will do the pack and the 
vehicle level testing. That is the next phase. So far, the performance testing has been very 
satisfactory. We got positive feedback. This is on the NMC side. On the LFP side, the 102 Ah 
LFP cells we are already making.

We have given it to some telecom operators for validation, as well as we have started using it in 
our e-rickshaw packs, which is our own pack. These packs have been delivered to the market, 
they are running, and we have got quite positive response on the performance of the LFP cell as 
well. We expect the various validations of both NMC two-wheeler OEMs as well as the telecom 
towers to close concurrently very soon. 
 
Meanwhile, we have also started supplying two-wheeler samples to some more OEMs beyond 
the leading OEMs. This is the status as of now. As of now, if you look at the market outlook, I

Currently, the two-wheeler market, you have seen last three months, Vahan registrations of

They have ramped up to about two lakh vehicles per month, which was roughly 1.2 lakh last

have adequately put up our capacity and we can take a share of the market, even not looking at

Pravin Saraf:

PLI scheme announced. We are waiting for the PLI, we will of course apply for the PLI. As 
under the PLI scheme, we will need to wait, and once the clarity is there, then we can go ahead

validations are showing positive results for BESS cell also. 
Avik Roy: 
Thank you, Pravin. 
Raghunandhan: 
Thank you, sir. My second question was on capital allocation. 
Avik Roy:

The core business generates strong cash and funds the new energy investments while staying

Avik Roy: 
So, at this moment, I think I have mentioned this before also, our capital allocation strategy 
revolves around three elements beyond the dividend payout. The first is protecting the core. 
Protecting the core has two elements. Every year, we invest close to our depreciation, which is 
about INR400 crore-INR500 crores every year on our core business.

That has been consistently which we have been doing in the past. But in the past, we were mostly 
investing on our manufacturing technology to improve productivity, to reduce cost. We will 
continue to do that. Today, we have added one more element, which is also debottlenecking our 
existing lead-acid capacity to cater to the market after two to three years. See, today is a unique 
sweet spot for lead-acid because both OEM as well as aftermarket is growing concurrently. In 
the past, it never used to happen like this. 
 
If the OEM was growing, aftermarket would be slow, aftermarket growing, OEM would be slow. 
Now we see both the segments growing strongly concurrently. Therefore, we are investing 
capital in debottlenecking each of our factory. Thankfully, we have multiple factories where

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Dr. Lal PathLabs' Q2 FY27
