opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you 
need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing 
star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being 
recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Nishid Solanki from CDR India. Thank you, 
and over to you sir. 
Nishid Solanki: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone, and welcome to Dr. Lal PathLabs Q2 & H1 
FY27 earnings conference call. Today, we are joined by senior members of the 
management team, including:  
• 
(Hony) Brig. Dr. Arvind Lal - Executive Chairman  
• 
Mr. Shankha Banerjee - CEO, and  
• 
Mr. Ved Prakash Goel, Group CFO and CEO, International Business 
 
I would like to share our standard disclaimer. Some of the statements made on 
today's conference call could be forward-looking in nature, and the actual results 
could vary from these forward-looking statements. A detailed statement in this regard 
is available in the results presentation, which has been circulated to you and also 
available on stock exchange website. 
 
I would now like to invite Dr. Lal to share his perspectives. Thank you, and over to 
you, sir. 
Arvind Lal: 
Thank you, Nishid. Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for joining 
us on our second quarter and half year earnings call for the financial year 2027.  
Indian healthcare system continues to focus on improving patient outcomes with 
diagnostics playing a significant role in anchoring evidence-based therapies. 
Advancement in diagnostic technology is going hand-in-hand with the increasing 
complexity of the demands from the clinical community for more precise and 
personalized therapies.  
Our recent acquisition of S N GeneLab in Surat adds differentiated tests to our 
portfolio in oncogenomics and reproductive genomics, which combined with our 

 
Page 3 of 18 
 
national reach will benefit the wider clinical community. S N GeneLab has a proven 
track record and an active R&D program in the genomics area with international tie-
ups and in-house research work. This will complement the R&D effort, which LPL 
has embarked upon with academic institutions and other research institutions. These 
efforts are aimed at leading the scientific development in diagnostics and introducing 
new tests and technologies in India. 
 
There is also an increasing emphasis on disease prevention and diagnostics has an 
important part to play in that shift. Under the National Program for Prevention and 
Control of Non-Communicable Diseases, that is (NP-NCDs) through 1.8 lakh 
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, over 41.5 crore people have been screened for 
hypertension, 41.3 crore for diabetes and 35.3 crore for oral cancer and 16.5 crore 
women for breast cancer and close to 8.7 crore women for cervical cancer. This is a 
public health effort of extraordinary ambition, but screening only is the beginning of 
a clinical journey. Every positive finding requires confirmation and then monitoring 
and that work is done in laboratories. The need for accurate, accredited, high-quality 
confirmatory diagnostics tests is only going to increase. 
 
Our expansion into the international markets has seen significant movement this 
quarter with the acquisition of Sunshine diagnostics in Ghana and a JV in 
Uzbekistan. These are small steps towards building a meaningful long-term business 
in markets where we can contribute towards improving the diagnostic ecosystem. 
 
Our team is also working to make quality diagnostics available to the communities in 
the underserved regions of our country. Our rural outreach program is gaining 
strength in the seven states that we have launched with higher patient numbers this 
quarter. The migration from unorganized to organized testing remains the defining 
opportunity of this decade, and it will be won on quality, reach and trust. 
 
With that, I hand over to Mr. Shankha Banerjee. Thank you very much.  
Shankha Banerjee: 
Thank you, Dr. Lal, and good evening, everybody.  
I am happy to share that we have sustained our growth momentum in Q2 FY27 with 
a revenue achievement of Rs. 874 crore at a 19.6% growth. This is the highest 
quarterly growth in the last 5 years and has been driven by a 9% growth in patient 
volumes. 
 
Our consistent focus on the key strategic pillars of scientific leadership, enhanced 
patient experience, and operational excellence are yielding results.  

 
Page 4 of 18 
 
Our commitment to medical leadership and clinical tests remains the primary engine 
driving our test mix and realization quality.  
• 
In Q2 FY27, we continue to expand our advanced testing portfolio and 
strengthened our diagnostic depth across specialized frontiers such as 
oncogenomics, transplant immunology and rare genetic disorders. 
Demonstrating this commitment, we launched around 140 new tests during 
H1 FY27 and 2 first in India assays in Q2 FY27.  
• 
Our recent acquisition of S N GeneLab strengthens our play in genomics 
testing. The combined portfolio with testing hubs in North and West 
strengthens our genomics expertise, broadens our advanced diagnostic 
portfolio, and enables deployment across our entire network.  
• 
We have rolled out a new physical patient report format, which enhances the 
reporting experience as it incorporates the trend chart of most common 
tests. It also has a useful anti-counterfeit watermark embedded to ensure 
genuineness of the report. These reports are now reaching more than 80% 
of our patients daily.  
• 
We have recently established an enterprise-wide foundation for digital 
pathology through a secure, scalable hybrid cloud platform that unifies 
image management, supports multiple file formats and integrates 
seamlessly with our LIMS solution. The platform is future-ready to enable 
multiple business streams, including AI-led services.  
The team is eager to build on the strong foundation of the first half and deliver our 
targeted sustainable revenue growth over the medium term. We continue to retain a 
significant pricing headroom as a strategic lever going forward. 
 
I will now hand over the call to Ved, who will take you through the detailed financial 
metrics of the quarter under review. Over to you, Ved. 
Ved Prakash Goel: 
Thank you, Shankha. Good evening, everyone, and a warm welcome. Thank you for 
joining us today. I will take you through the financial highlights for the quarter under 
review.  
We continue to build on our strong operational momentum, focusing on growth, 
customer engagement and expanding our presence across the diagnostic 
landscape. Growth was anchored by solid operational metrics. Sample volume 
expanded by 13.6% to 28.8 million, while patient volume grew 9% to 9 million this 
quarter.  

 
Page 5 of 18 
 
Let me take you through the key financial highlights for Q2 and first half FY27.  
• 
Revenue for Q2 FY27 came in at Rs. 874 crore compared to Rs. 731 crore 
in the same quarter last year, reflecting a growth of 19.6%. The first half 
FY27 revenue stood at Rs. 1,672 crore, marking a growth of 19.4%. 
• 
Revenue per patient for Q2 FY27 came in at Rs. 976,  which is 9.7% higher 
compared to Rs. 889 in Q2 FY26.  
• 
EBITDA for Q2 FY27 came in at Rs. 280 crore compared to Rs. 224 crore 
in Q2 FY26 registering a growth of 25.1% with an EBITDA margin of 32.1%.  
• 
EBITDA for first half of FY27 stood at Rs. 528 crore versus Rs. 416 crore in 
H1 FY26, registering a growth of 26.7% with EBITDA margin of 31.6%.  
• 
PBT for Q2 FY27 came in at Rs. 261 crore registering a growth of 28.1% 
with a PBT margin of 29.8%. First half PBT of FY27 stood at Rs. 489 crore

• 
PAT for Q2 FY27 came in at Rs. 194 crore compared to Rs. 152 crore in the

•

•

• 
Our commitment to operational excellence is reflecting in our efficient 
working capital management with a net working capital remaining negative

capital allocation.  
•

•

expansion initiatives:

o 
We have completed the acquisition of SN GeneLab Private Limited. This 
acquisition will strengthen our expertise in genomics and broaden our 
portfolio of advanced diagnostic services.  
o

recorded highest ever physical performance in any quarter by posting total handling volume of 
1,448,379 TEUs. We have posted highest ever operating turnover at INR2,373 crores and 
highest ever total income in any quarter, INR2,466 crores. The revenue growth has been 0.93%.

handsome results. Throughput in the H1 in the EXIM segment has increased by 4.57% and

Ladies and gentlemen, welcoming you to the Container Corporation of India Limited Q2 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call hosted by DAM Capital Advisors Limited. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. 
Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star 
then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now 
hand the conference over to Mr. Kunal Shah. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Shah. 
Kunal Shah: 
Yes. Good afternoon. Welcome to the 2Q F27 Earnings Call of Container Corporation of India. 
We have the management being represented by Mr. Ajit Kumar, the Chairman and Managing 
Director. I would like to hand over the call to Ajit sir for his opening remarks, post which we 
can take up the Q&A. Thanks, and over to you sir. 
Ajit Kumar Panda: 
Good morning, Mr. Kunal, and good morning to all the participants who have joined this 
conference call. Along with me, we have got the management team, Mr. Vijoy Singh, our 
Director, International Marketing and Operations; Mr. Vivek Gupta, Director (Finance); 
Principal Executive Director (Finance) and Company Secretary, Mr. Harish Chandra. 
And our Group General Manager, International Marketing, Mr. Paresh Agarwal. So you are now 
welcome to ask your questions. Before you ask the questions, I will give my opening remarks. 
I'm very happy to announce a fairly decent results under very challenging geopolitical 
circumstances. 
 
CONCOR has demonstrated remarkable resilience amidst the adverse circumstances. We have 
recorded highest ever physical performance in any quarter by posting total handling volume of 
1,448,379 TEUs. We have posted highest ever operating turnover at INR2,373 crores and 
highest ever total income in any quarter, INR2,466 crores. The revenue growth has been 0.93%. 
We have announced a dividend of INR1.9 per share, and the total dividend has now gone up to 
INR3.5 per share in the first half. 
 
We have also reported handsome profits. The profits -- stand-alone profit before tax has been 
INR462 crores, that is amounting INR154 crores per month, a very remarkable performance 
given the adverse circumstances through which we have gone. As all of you are aware, a 
ceasefire, which was announced in the Gulf, it collapsed in a few days and the Strait of Hormuz 
for container traffic remains practically closed. 
The ports, which were the engines of trade in West Asia, they are not handling that. The trade 
has shifted to new ports of Khor Fakkan and Fujairah. And also our ports on both on the Western 
side and Eastern side, they are doing handling. They are doing transhipment of cargo, which 
used to be transhipped in the ports of the Gulf region. 
Therefore, there has been lots of turbulence in the trade. But despite that, we have posted 
handsome results. Throughput in the H1 in the EXIM segment has increased by 4.57% and 
domestic segment, 4.22%, total 4.48%.

November 03, 2026

a-vis corresponding lead of 686 kilometers in the Q2 of last year. In the domestic segment, our 
lead has gone up to from 13 -- to 1,315 kilometers from 1,298 kilometers last year. The average 
lead in Q2 has increased to 817 kilometers from 779 kilometers, that is an increase of 4.9%. Our 
Nepal business has increased from 45 rakes to 107 rakes in this quarter, 138% increase. 
 
Bulk cement in tank containers, it has continued to increase. In this quarter, we have added 195

Dear Sir / Madam, 
 
In furtherance to our intimation dated November 5, 2026, we wish to inform you that the Board of 
Directors (“Board”) of IIFL Finance Limited (“Company”) at their meeting held today i.e. Tuesday, 
November 10, 2026, has inter alia considered and approved the following: 
 
1. 
Re-classification and increase of authorised share capital of the Company and consequent 
alteration of capital clause of the Memorandum of Association of the Company 
 
Subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company, the Board has approved the increase in 
the authorised share capital of the Company from INR 971,05,00,000 (Indian Rupees Nine Hundred 
and Seventy-One Crore Five Lakh) divided into 235,52,50,000 (Two Hundred and Thirty-Five Crore 
Fifty-Two Lakh Fifty Thousand) equity shares having face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two) each and 
50,00,00,000 (Fifty Crore) preference shares having face value of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each, to 
INR 5621,05,00,146 (Indian Rupees Five Thousand Six Hundred and Twenty-One Crore Five Lakh One 
Hundred and Forty-Six) divided into 235,52,50,000 (Two Hundred and Thirty-Five Crore Fifty-Two Lakh 
Fifty Thousand) equity shares having face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two) each and 8,55,48,173 
(Eight Crore Fifty-Five Lakh Forty-Eight Thousand One Hundred and Seventy-Three) preference shares 
having face value of INR 602 (Indian Rupees Six Hundred and Two) each. 
 
Consequently, the capital clause (Clause V) of the Memorandum of Association of the Company shall 
be amended, subject to approval by shareholders of the Company and any other statutory/ regulatory 
approvals, as may be required under the provisions of applicable law. 
 
2. 
Issuance of compulsorily convertible preference shares and warrants by way of preferential 
issue on a private placement basis

statutory/ regulatory authorities, as may be required, the Board has approved the issuance of: (i)

Re.: Regulation 30 and other applicable provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India

Dear Sir / Madam, 
 
In furtherance to our intimation dated November 5, 2026, we wish to inform you that the Board of 
Directors (“Board”) of IIFL Finance Limited (“Company”) at their meeting held today i.e. Tuesday, 
November 10, 2026, has inter alia considered and approved the following: 
 
1. 
Re-classification and increase of authorised share capital of the Company and consequent 
alteration of capital clause of the Memorandum of Association of the Company 
 
Subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company, the Board has approved the increase in 
the authorised share capital of the Company from INR 971,05,00,000 (Indian Rupees Nine Hundred 
and Seventy-One Crore Five Lakh) divided into 235,52,50,000 (Two Hundred and Thirty-Five Crore 
Fifty-Two Lakh Fifty Thousand) equity shares having face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two) each and 
50,00,00,000 (Fifty Crore) preference shares having face value of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each, to 
INR 5621,05,00,146 (Indian Rupees Five Thousand Six Hundred and Twenty-One Crore Five Lakh One 
Hundred and Forty-Six) divided into 235,52,50,000 (Two Hundred and Thirty-Five Crore Fifty-Two Lakh 
Fifty Thousand) equity shares having face value of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two) each and 8,55,48,173 
(Eight Crore Fifty-Five Lakh Forty-Eight Thousand One Hundred and Seventy-Three) preference shares 
having face value of INR 602 (Indian Rupees Six Hundred and Two) each. 
 
Consequently, the capital clause (Clause V) of the Memorandum of Association of the Company shall 
be amended, subject to approval by shareholders of the Company and any other statutory/ regulatory 
approvals, as may be required under the provisions of applicable law. 
 
2. 
Issuance of compulsorily convertible preference shares and warrants by way of preferential 
issue on a private placement basis 
 
Subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company and receipt of approvals from applicable 
statutory/ regulatory authorities, as may be required, the Board has approved the issuance of: (i) 
8,55,48,173 compulsorily convertible preference shares, having face value of INR 602 (Indian Rupees 
Six Hundred and Two) each, and (ii) 2,10,00,000 warrants by way of preferential issue on a private 
placement basis in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, and the rules made 
thereunder (“Act”), Chapter V of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2018 (“SEBI ICDR Regulations”) and other applicable laws to the proposed allottees as set out in the

modify, substitute and insert certain articles, and adoption of the amended and restated AOA 
and grant of special rights to Investor 1 
 
Subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company, the Board has approved the amendment 
to the AOA for (a) inserting a new Article 13A (immediately following the existing Article 13, and 
immediately preceding existing Article 14) and (b) deleting and substituting the existing Article 13, for 
enabling/ empowering the Company to issue warrants and/or other convertible securities on a 
preferential basis and to issue compulsorily convertible preference shares on such terms (including as 
to mandatory and preferential payment of dividend, conversion and other matters) as determined by 
the Board.  
 
Further, subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company and in compliance with the Listing 
Regulations and the Act, the Board has approved the amendment of the AOA to incorporate relevant 
terms of the Subscription Agreement 1, and to adopt such amended and restated AOA with effect 
from the date of completion under the Subscription Agreement 1 (“Restated Articles”), in substitution 
for and to the exclusion of the existing AOA. Further, certain rights proposed to be granted to the 
Investor 1 may qualify as special rights under Regulation 31B of the Listing Regulations and are also 
subject to approval of the shareholders of the Company. The disclosures in respect of proposed 
amendments to the AOA, in brief, are set out in Annexure I. The brief details of the rights and 
obligations of Investor 1 being incorporated in the Restated Articles are set out in point 5 of Annexure

Earnings Conference Call hosted by Investec Capital Services India Private Limited. As a

for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the 
conference call, please signal an operator by pressing “*” then “0” on your touch-tone phone. 
Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Anshuman Gupta from Investec Capital Services (India) 
Private Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Anshuman Gupta: 
Thank you very much, operator, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm Anshuman Gupta from 
Investec, and I cover pharma and health care space at Investec. So welcome all of you to the Q2 
FY27 earnings call of Global Health Limited.  
From the management side, we have with us today Dr. Naresh Trehan, Chairman and Managing 
Director; Mr. Pankaj Sahni, Group CEO and Director; Mr. Yogesh Kumar Gupta, Chief 
Financial Officer; Mr. Gaurav Chugh, Head of Investor Relations. The discussion today may 
include certain forward-looking statements and the safe harbor notice set out in the company's 
presentation also applies to this conference call. A transcript of this call will also be available on 
the company's website. 
 
With this, I would like to hand over the conference call to Dr. Trehan for his opening remarks. 
Thank you, and over to you, Doctor. 
Naresh Trehan: 
Thank you. Good afternoon to all of you. Thank you for joining us today for Medanta's Q2 and 
H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. I hope all of you have had the chance to review the results 
and presentations that were released yesterday.  
At Medanta, our journey has always been guided by a simple belief, access to the highest 
standard of healthcare should not be determined by where the patient lives. Our responsibility is 
to bring world-class clinical expertise, advanced technologies and compassionate care closer to 
the people who need it. 
 
We have delivered a strong performance this quarter. We witnessed a healthy growth in patient 
volumes, supported by increasing demand across all our specialties, a growing proportion of 
complex cases and the continued trust of patients and referring doctors. This trust has been built 
over time through clinical outcomes, the depth of our medical expertise and confidence patients 
place in our institution. 
 
I'm pleased to share that our 550-bed Noida hospital inaugurated in November 2025, achieved 
EBITDA breakeven during the quarter, within a year of its inauguration. This is an important 
milestone demonstrating the successful ramp-up of the hospital, improving operating leverage 
and the scalability of the Medanta model. It reinforces our confidence in replicating this model 
across new geographies. 

 
 
 
 
Global Health Limited – Medanta 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 17 
 
 
We continue to invest in technologies and specialized infrastructure that expand the boundaries 
of what our clinicians can achieve. During the quarter, we added the Siemens ARTIS icono 
biplane system at our Gurugram hospital. At Patna, we strengthened our capabilities with the 
Siemens ARTIS ceiling-mounted cath lab and the VELYS hip navigation system. During the 
quarter, we onboarded more than 100 doctors, including over 65 clinicians across specialties.  
During the quarter, we also took an important step towards expanding our presence in the Delhi 
NCR region. We acquired a 2.61-acre land parcel in Ghaziabad through an e-auction, where we 
plan to develop a 500-bed multi-specialty hospital. The hospital will strengthen our presence in 
the Delhi NCR's healthcare system. It will also bring high-quality tertiary and quaternary care 
to Ghaziabad's fast-growing population and the surrounding catchment. We see Ghaziabad as 
an attractive health care destination. It has a large growing population, witnessing rapid 
urbanization, expanding residential and commercial developments and strong connectivity with 
Delhi NCR. We believe it is well suited for a Medanta hospital.  
Including Ghaziabad, our expansion pipeline comprises of 6 new greenfield hospitals, 
supporting our ambition to double our bed capacity over time. Our focus is not simply on adding 
capacity, but on taking the Medanta model of high-quality, advanced healthcare to more 
geographies, particularly those where access to comprehensive specialized care remains limited. 
 
The progress at Noida gives us confidence in the strength of this model. And as we expand, we 
will remain focused on disciplined execution, maintaining the highest standard of care and 
building institutions that earn the trust of the communities they serve. Ultimately, our purpose 
remains unchanged: to touch more lives through clinical excellence, innovation and 
compassionate care. This is the vision that will continue to guide Medanta's journey. 
 
With all these details that I just shared with you, I will hand over the call to Mr. Pankaj Sahni, 
our Group CEO, who will take you through the strategic, operational and financial performance 
of the quarter. So over to you, Pankaj. 
Pankaj Sahni: 
Thank you, Dr. Trehan. Good afternoon and thank you for joining us today.  
Q2 FY27 has been a strong quarter for Medanta, with robust growth across financial and 
operational parameters. We have continued to build on the momentum across our network, with 
improving operating performance and a meaningful contribution from both our Cluster 1 and 
Cluster 2 hospitals. 
 
Let me take you through the key financial and operational developments for the quarter. Before 
we get to the numbers, I would like to point out that we have modified the reporting of a few 
financial metrics in our investor presentation to provide greater transparency and a more 
meaningful understanding of our core operating business performance. This format is also 
aligned with the majority of the analyst reports. We have now started reporting revenue as 
revenue from operations and EBITDA as operating EBITDA. Revenue from operations does not 
include other income, which is primarily interest income. 

 
 
 
 
Global Health Limited – Medanta 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 17 
 
 
Operating EBITDA is defined as EBITDA, excluding other income and after accounting for 
ESOP expenses. The comparative figures in the investor presentation and the press release have 
also been presented on a consistent like-for-like basis. 
 
Now coming to the financial performance. Consolidated revenue from operations for the quarter 
was INR 14,690 million, representing a healthy growth of 34% year-on-year. Operating 
EBITDA grew 60% year-on-year to INR 3,701 million, with improved margins of 25.2% in Q2 
FY27 compared to 21% in Q2 FY26. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR 2,191 million 
compared to INR1,584 million in Q2 FY26, representing a year-on-year growth of 38%. 
 
Coming to our balance sheet and cash position. As of September 30, 2026, Medanta had a net 
cash surplus of INR 7,815 million compared to a net cash surplus of INR 5,906 million as of 
March 31, 2026. We continued to generate strong operating cash flows, with operating cash 
flows for H1 FY27 amounting to INR 5,678 million. 
 
Operationally, we continued to witness robust momentum across the network. Inpatient volumes 
increased by 30% year-on-year, while outpatient volumes grew by 38%, reflecting sustained 
demand across our specialties and the continued scale-up of our newer facilities. Occupied bed 
days increased by 22% with network occupancy improving to 67% on expanded bed capacity 
compared to 64% in Q2 FY26. 
 
Overall, our census bed capacity increased to 3,115 in Q2 FY27 from 2,658 beds in Q2 FY26, a 
growth of 17%. While our total bed capacity stood at 3,811 in Q2 FY27 compared to 3,435 in 
Q2 FY26. Average revenue per patient, ARPP, increased by 3% year-on-year to INR 2.06 lakhs, 
supported by favorable case mix and increasing contribution from high-acuity specialties. 
 
Average length of stay, or ALOS, for the quarter was 2.89 days compared to 3.06 days in the 
same quarter last year. International patient revenue grew by 30% year-on-year to INR 993 
million, reflecting strong demand from key international markets. Our OPD pharmacy business 
continues to witness strong growth trajectory, with revenue increasing 53% year-on-year to  
INR 699 million, supported by both hospital pharmacies and our expanding retail pharmacy 
network. 
 
On the capacity and infrastructure front, during the quarter, we added 74 beds, which includes 
49 beds at Noida and 25 beds at Lucknow, taking our operational bed capacity to 3,811 beds. In 
addition, we also continued to strengthen our clinical and procedural capabilities. Medanta 
Ranchi added Medanta medical oncology services, while Medanta Gurugram added 2 new 
operating theatres and 1 new biplane cath lab during the quarter. As we speak, we will be adding 
6 new operating theatres and 2 new cath labs at Medanta Gurugram, 4 new operating theatres 
and 1 new cath lab at Patna and 5 new operating theatres at our Lucknow facility over the next 
couple of quarters. 
 
I now turn to Medanta Noida. As we had indicated previously, we are pleased to inform you that 
Medanta Noida achieved EBITDA breakeven in Q2 FY27, posting revenue from operations of 
INR 1,059 million and operating EBITDA of INR 86 million for the quarter. This improvement 

 
 
 
 
Global Health Limited – Medanta 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 17 
 
reflects the continued scale-up of operations and increasing patient volumes at our Noida 
hospital. 
 
During the quarter, we added 49 beds, taking the total operational bed capacity to 482 beds. Our 
focus remains on establishing Medanta Noida as another flagship institution with comprehensive 
clinical capabilities, high standards of patient care and the ability to serve the growing health 
care needs of the region. 
 
Now coming to the cluster-wise performance. Our hospital business is divided into 2 clusters 
and the following cluster-wise performance analysis relates exclusively to the hospital business 
of the company.  
Cluster 1 hospital, which includes Medanta Gurugram, Indore and Ranchi. Revenue from 
operations for Cluster 1 stood at INR 8,229 million, registering a year-on-year growth of 18%. 
The operating EBITDA stood at INR 1,810 million, reflecting a strong growth of 29% year-on-
year, with improved margins of 22%. 
 
The performance was supported by a 15% increase in inpatient volumes, reflecting sustained 
demand. ARPP of Cluster 1 increased by 2%, driven by a favorable specialty on payer mix. 
Average length of stay reduced to 2.80 days from 2.98 days, while occupancy improved to 66% 
from 61% in Q2 FY26, reflecting improved utilization of our existing health care infrastructure. 
Overall, Cluster 1 continues to witness steady growth while delivering strong operating cash 
flow. 
 
Turning to Cluster 2, comprising Lucknow, Patna and Noida. This cluster continues to witness 
robust growth. Revenue from operations increased by 63% year-on-year to INR 5,790 million 
from INR 3,547 million in Q2 FY26, driven by ramp-up of Noida facility and continuing growth 
momentum in Lucknow and Patna facilities. Operating EBITDA increased by 110% to  
INR 1,837 million, driven by EBITDA breakeven of Noida facility. Noida had an EBITDA loss 
of INR 199 million in Q2 FY26 and robust operational performance of Lucknow and Patna. 
 
Overall, the Cluster 2 hospitals witnessed a 52% increase in inpatient volumes, while occupied 
bed days increased by 43%, reflecting continued capacity utilization across the hospitals. ARPP 
grew by 8%, supported by favorable case and specialty mix across the network. Cluster 2 
occupancy stood at 67% in Q2 FY27 compared to 62% in the same quarter last year, driven by 
strong inpatient volume growth across all 3 facilities. 
 
Let me now brief you on our new Ghaziabad hospital project. As Dr. Trehan mentioned and as 
you would be aware, Medanta has been allotted a land parcel of approximately 2.6 acres at 
Siddharth Vihar Yojna in Ghaziabad. We secured the parcel on a freehold basis through an 
online auction at a value of INR 166 crores. Yesterday, our Board has approved a 500-bed 
hospital project with a total capex of approximately INR 1,000 crores. 
 
The proposed hospital will further strengthen our presence in the Delhi NCR health care 
ecosystem and expand access to high-quality tertiary and quaternary care for Ghaziabad's rapidly 
growing population and the surrounding catchment area. We see Ghaziabad as a compelling 

 
 
 
 
Global Health Limited – Medanta 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 17 
 
health care market, supported by a large and growing population, rapid urbanization, expanding 
residential and commercial development and strong connectivity across Delhi NCR. 
 
The city also serves as an important catchment for patients from Eastern Delhi, Meerut, 
Saharanpur, Hapur, Bulandshahr and the wider Western UP region. We believe this hospital will 
complement our existing facilities in Gurugram and Noida, while enabling us to serve a distinct 
and expanding catchment across Ghaziabad and Western Uttar Pradesh. 
 
As far as our capacity expansion goes, we have a significant bed addition pipeline that is 
expected to add approximately 3,450 beds over the next few years. This represents almost a 
doubling of our network capacity to over 7,600 beds. To support this expansion, we have 
outlined a planned capital expenditure of over INR 6,000 crores over the next 4 to 5 years. This 
includes investments in our upcoming hospitals, capacity expansion at existing facilities and 
supporting infrastructure. 
 
To conclude, we remain confident in Medanta's growth trajectory. Our strategy remains centered 
on 3 key priorities: strengthening our existing hospitals, accelerating the scale-up of our 
developing hospitals and executing against our expansion pipeline. We believe our growing 
network, expanding clinical capabilities and strong financial position provide a solid foundation 
for sustainable growth and long-term value creation for our shareholders. 
 
With that, I would now like to request the operator to open the line for questions. Thank you.

the Delhi NCR's healthcare system. It will also bring high-quality tertiary and quaternary care

geographies, particularly those where access to comprehensive specialized care remains limited.

compassionate care. This is the vision that will continue to guide Medanta's journey.

demand across our specialties and the continued scale-up of our newer facilities. Occupied bed 
days increased by 22% with network occupancy improving to 67% on expanded bed capacity 
compared to 64% in Q2 FY26.

supported by favorable case mix and increasing contribution from high-acuity specialties.

same quarter last year. International patient revenue grew by 30% year-on-year to INR 993 
million, reflecting strong demand from key international markets. Our OPD pharmacy business 
continues to witness strong growth trajectory, with revenue increasing 53% year-on-year to  
INR 699 million, supported by both hospital pharmacies and our expanding retail pharmacy 
network.

Regulations, 2015, as amended ("the LODR Regulations").

Emphasis of Matter 
6.1 Suspension of Construction of Two Passenger Vessels and Related 
Uncertainties 
In 2016, the Holding Company entered into a contract with the Administration 
of a Union Territory of India for the construction of two passenger vessels at a 
total contract value of Rs.81,900 lakhs (excluding taxes and foreign exchange 
variation). The vessels were launched in January 2020 and August 2022, 
respectively. 
As at the reporting date, approximately 55% of the construction work, up to the 
fourth stage, has been completed and payments aggregating to Rs.66,504 lakhs 
have been received from the Administration. The fifth and final stage is linked 
to delivery of the vessels. 
Subsequently, the said Administration of a Union Territory has expressed its 
intention to take delivery of one vessel, while the other vessel is proposed to be 
taken over by another Administration of a Union Territory, both subject to 
certain reconfigurations. However, the scope of modifications and related 
commercial terms, including reimbursement of costs, are yet to be finalised 
between the parties. Pending receipt of the necessary approvals and finalisation 
of the commercial arrangements, further construction activities remain 
suspended. 
Accordingly, the Holding Company expressed its inability to determine the 
financial impact, if any, arising from factors such as ageing of the vessels due to 
prolonged inactivity, occupation of berthing space and costs of bank guarantees 
amounting to Rs.1,12,412 lakhs furnished to the Administration, which remain 
pending for renewal as at March 31, 2026. The comparative figures for the 
previous quarter ended June 30, 2026, are identical to those of the current 
reporting period. (Refer Note No.5 to the unaudited consolidated financial 
results).

6.1 Suspension of Construction of Two Passenger Vessels and Related 
Uncertainties 
In 2016, the Holding Company entered into a contract with the Administration 
of a Union Territory of India for the construction of two passenger vessels at a 
total contract value of Rs.81,900 lakhs (excluding taxes and foreign exchange 
variation). The vessels were launched in January 2020 and August 2022, 
respectively. 
As at the reporting date, approximately 55% of the construction work, up to the 
fourth stage, has been completed and payments aggregating to Rs.66,504 lakhs 
have been received from the Administration. The fifth and final stage is linked 
to delivery of the vessels. 
Subsequently, the said Administration of a Union Territory has expressed its 
intention to take delivery of one vessel, while the other vessel is proposed to be 
taken over by another Administration of a Union Territory, both subject to 
certain reconfigurations. However, the scope of modifications and related 
commercial terms, including reimbursement of costs, are yet to be finalised 
between the parties. Pending receipt of the necessary approvals and finalisation 
of the commercial arrangements, further construction activities remain 
suspended. 
Accordingly, the Holding Company expressed its inability to determine the 
financial impact, if any, arising from factors such as ageing of the vessels due to 
prolonged inactivity, occupation of berthing space and costs of bank guarantees 
amounting to Rs.1,12,412 lakhs furnished to the Administration, which remain 
pending for renewal as at March 31, 2026. The comparative figures for the 
previous quarter ended June 30, 2026, are identical to those of the current 
reporting period. (Refer Note No.5 to the unaudited consolidated financial 
results).

5. The holding Company is executing shipbuilding contracts with the Andaman & Nicobar Administration (A&N) for the 
construction of two 1200-passenger vessels (yard nos. SH.0023 and SH.0024). The contractual delivery dates, as extended, 
have expired for both vessels as on 29 April 2023 for vessel SH.0023, and 30 October 2023 for vessel SH.0024. 
The two vessels are customized and designed for specific operations between Andaman Islands and Main Land. Subsequently 
based on a request from the A&N Administration, the holding Company has abated delivery activity, as the Administration has 
sought reallocation of the vessels to other prospective buyers. However, such reallocation would necessitate significant 
technical modifications and cost, and the vessels, in their current state, are considered to have no alternative use. 
Given that the holding Company continues to have a valid and enforceable contract with the A&N Administration, and there is 
no current mutual termination or novation of the contract, no additional provision for Liquidated Damages (LD) has been 
recognized beyond 29 April 2023 and 30 October 2023, respectively, for SH.0023 and SH.0024 for reason of abated delivery at 
the request of the buyer. In accordance with the terms of the contract and based on prudent estimates, the holding Company 
has recognized provision for LD up to the aforementioned dates. 
The cumulative percentage of completion for the two vessels as on 30.09.2026 is 54.84 percent for SH.0023 and 55.19 
percent for SH.0024. The total liquidated damages for SH.0023 is Rs. 11814.08 Lakhs and for SH.0024 is Rs. 9756.34 Lakhs 
up to September 30, 2026. The holding Company has recognized revenue to the tune of Rs. 16946.32 Lakhs towards SH.0023 
and Rs. 17161.87 Lakhs towards SH.0024 upto 30.09.2026 after considering the liquidated damages. 
In line with the above, and given that the request for reallocation, the holding Company is now actively engaged in discussions 
with the Andaman & Nicobar Administration (A&N) and the Union Territory of Lakshadweep Administration (UTLA), under the 
guidance of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. These discussions are focused on modifying the two vessels to suit 
the present requirements of either administration. Both administrations have confirmed their willingness to take over each 
vessel in its current under-construction state, subject to the necessary modifications. The holding Company continues to 
monitor developments related to this contract and will review its accounting estimates and provisioning requirements in 
subsequent periods as more information becomes available.

Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call

Moderator 
Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. I am Karthikeyan, moderator for the conference call. Welcome 
to NBCC (India) Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. We have with us today Shri K. P. 
Mahadevaswamy, Chairman-cum-Managing Director; Dr. Suman Kumar, Director (Commercial), Shri. 
Anjeev Kumar Jain, Director (Finance); Shri. Ashutosh Gautam, Director (Projects); and Mr. Sri M.B. 
Singhal, Executive Director (Finance).  
As a reminder, all participants will be in listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to 
ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference 
call, please signal an operator by pressing * and then 0 on your touch-tone telephone. Please note this 
conference is being recorded.  
I would now like to hand over the floor to Shri. K. P. Mahadevaswamy, sir. Thank you, and over to you, 
sir. 
K. P. Mahadevaswamy 
Thank you, Mr. Karthikeyan. Good morning, everyone. A hearty welcome to all of you. First of all, 
Happy Dhanteras, and wish you a Happy Deepavali in advance. Before starting off call, we welcome 
our new Director (Projects), Shri. Ashutosh Gautam. He has been serving for more than 34 years in 
multidisciplinary wings of infrastructure, which will help NBCC in multiple fronts.  
For Q2 operation and execution, we have achieved a revenue from operation of INR 2,890 crores 
standalone and INR 3,396 crores on consolidated, reflecting a 38% YoY increase on standalone basis. 
On standalone basis, EBITDA increased significantly by 154% INR 219 crores from INR 86 crores. And 
our standalone PAT increased by 31%, stands at INR 225 crores, marking a significant growth.  
For H1 operation and execution, we have achieved a revenue of operation INR 4,713 crores standalone 
INR 5,655 crores on consolidated, reflecting 26% YoY increase on standalone basis. On standalone 
basis, EBITDA increased significantly by 105%, INR 379 crores from INR 183 crores. Our standalone 
PAT stands at INR 376 crores, marking a significant 31% YoY growth. In terms of order book position, 
NBCC's standalone order book is standing at INR 1,12,000 crores and consolidated order book INR 
1,26,000 crore.  
New business secured in Q2 stands INR 3,600 crore on a consolidated basis and following are the 
major projects secured in last quarter. RBI Residential Complex at Amaravati, AP, New Andhra 
Pradesh, valuing INR 800 crores, Housing Project at Seychelles valuing around INR 600 crores. 
Business awarded to contractors: In Q2, we have awarded INR 1,500 crores of new tenders on 
consolidated level, which makes a total of INR 3,200 crores H1 in FY26-27. In next two quarters, we 
are expecting INR 15000-16,000 crore of new work will be awarded. Tenders of all the package of 
Supertech have been uploaded worth of INR 9,600 crores and will be awarded in this Q3 itself, and 
turnover will start from Q4. And many more projects including recently secured government of Bihar, 
West Bengal, J&K will be awarded in the upcoming quarters. 

 
3 
NBCC (India) Limited 
Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
 
06.11.2026 
Redevelopment projects: In continuation of sale/resource mobilization under 7 GPRA project, NBCC 
successfully sold residential apartments of 8.8 lakh square feet area at Avenue Towers, opposite to 
Leela hotel, Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi through an open e-auction at a total sale value of INR 5,191 
crores. All major packages in the redevelopment projects are in the running stage. Currently, it has 
INR 9,200 crores of balance workload.  
Amrapali Projects: Phase II of the Amrapali Project has started in different packages, and currently, 
there's INR 8,000 crores of balance workload. We are happy to share that NBCC has completed 24 
Amrapali projects of Phase I, and now handing over is in progress. Amrapali Phase II works are 
progressing on fast track, and at one of the packages, the building site has reached up to 26 floors. 
And in the last, to update about the HSCC merger, it is on fast track so that we would have better 
synergy. Thank you. Now the forum is open for the question and answer.  
Moderator 
Thank you, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you have 
a question, please press * and 1 on your telephone keypad and wait for your turn to ask a question. If 
you would like to withdraw your request, you may do so by pressing * and 1 again. Ladies and 
gentlemen, we will wait for a moment while the question queue assembles.  
First question comes from the line of Pankaj Kumar from Kotak Neo. Please go ahead. 
Pankaj Kumar 
Thanks for taking my question. Congrats on good set of numbers. Sir, in terms of guidance that we 
had given for FY27 earlier, around INR 13,000-14,000 crores of standalone revenue. And with H1, we 
have reached around INR 4,700 crores. So where are we in terms of achieving this guidance? And how 
is the way forward for FY28 and ’29?  
K. P. Mahadevaswamy 
I'm assuring we will achieve INR 13,000-14,000 on standalone basis. Usually, our first and second 
quarter will be in a slow pace. Second, third and fourth quarter only, we're going to achieve this figure. 
It holds good. We're going to achieve INR 13,000-14,000 crores on standalone basis.  
Pankaj Kumar 
And how about '28 and '29? 
K. P. Mahadevaswamy 
'FY29, already we have committed around INR 21,000 crores in consolidated-level basis, and 20-25% 
growth will be there, standalone as well.  
Pankaj Kumar 
This is for FY28 next year, you're saying, no? '29? 
K. P. Mahadevaswamy 
Yes.

About IRB Group: 
IRB Group is India’s leading and largest integrated infrastructure assets platform in the roads and 
highways sector, with a current portfolio of 27 revenue-generating highway assets aggregating to approx. 
₹940Bn across 13 Indian states. With approximately 1.5 million vehicle crossings daily across its assets, 
the Group accounts for nearly one-tenth of India’s total toll revenue. 
 
Having successfully completed its asset creation phase, the Group has entered a cash-harvesting phase, 
supported by its InvIT monetization strategy and sponsor-led operating leverage. With a weighted average 

Press Release 
3 
 
residual concession life of approximately 21 years, the portfolio provides strong visibility of long-term 
cashflows through predictable toll revenues, recurring O&M income and growing InvIT distributions.  
 
The Group has a clear roadmap to expand its asset base to approximately ₹1,400Bn by FY2030 with asset 
churn strategy and reinvesting proceeds into new opportunities to drive sustainable growth and long-
term value creation. 
 
IRB Infrastructure Trust (“Private InvIT”):  
 
IRB Infrastructure Trust is an Infrastructure Investment Trust sponsored by IRB Infrastructure Developers 
Limited under the SEBI’s Infrastructure Investment Trusts Regulations 2014. Private InvIT, pursuant to the 
Concessions granted by the respective Nodal Agencies, operates and manages 14 highway assets having 
9,525 Lane Kms and Enterprise Value of approx. ₹68,300Crs in the States of Maharashtra, Rajasthan, 
Gujarat, Goa, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, and Odisha. The 
Weighted Average Life of these Assets is 20 Years plus. Private InvIT is listed on NSE since 2023 under 
ticker “IRBIT”. For more information on Private InvIT, please visit www.irbinfratrust.co.in 
 
IRB InvIT Fund (“Public InvIT) : 
 
IRB InvIT Fund is the first Infrastructure Investment Trust sponsored by IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd 
and is registered under the SEBI’s Infrastructure Investment Trust Regulations 2014. Public InvIT, in 
pursuant to the Concessions granted by the respective Nodal Agencies, operates and manages 10 
highways assets, including 9 BOT and 2 HAM projects with 5,314 Lane Kms and Enterprise Value of 
approx. ₹23,000Crs in the States of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, 
Haryana and Uttar Pradesh. The Weighted Average Life of these Assets is 17 years plus. Public InvIT is 
listed on NSE & BSE since 2017 under ticker “IRBN” AND “IRBINVIT” respectively. For more information 
on Public InvIT, please visit www.irbinvit.co.in

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Metropolis Healthcare Limited Q2 and H1 
FY27 Earnings Conference Call, hosted by BNP Paribas. This conference call may contain 
forward-looking statements about the company, which are based on the beliefs, opinions and 
expectations of the company as on date of this call. These statements are not the guarantees of 
future performance and involve risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict. 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode. There will be an opportunity 
for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need any assistance during 
this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star and then zero on your touch-tone 
phones. Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to 
Mr. Tausif Shaikh. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Shaikh. 
Tausif Shaikh: 
Good morning, everyone. I welcome you all for the Metropolis Healthcare 2Q FY27 first half 
earnings con-call. I, Tausif Shaikh, India analyst at BNP Paribas for Pharma and Healthcare, 
would like to thank the management for giving us the opportunity for hosting the call. From the 
Metropolis team, we have the senior management led by Ameera Shah, Chairperson, Whole 
Time Director; Surendran Chemmenkotil, Managing Director; Sameer Patel, Chief Financial 
Officer; and Mohan Menon, Chief Marketing Officer. Now I will hand the call to Ameera ma'am 
for opening remarks. Over to you, ma'am. 
Ameera Shah: 
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today for the Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call of Metropolis Healthcare. I'm joined by Suren, Managing Director; Sameer 
Patel, CFO; Mohan Menon, CMO and the rest of our leadership team, along with SGA, our 
Investor Relations partner. We've uploaded our investor presentation on the exchanges and the 
website. I hope all of you have had a chance to go through it. 
Let me start with the headlines for the first half. For the past 2 years, our growth was around 
12% to 13% organically per year. However, over the last 4 to 6 quarters, we have stepped that 
up to 15% to 16% with revenue growing at 16.2% for H1 FY27, ahead of our stated guidance.  
Importantly, we have delivered the step-up in growth while expanding EBITDA margins by 190 
basis points to 26.2% EBITDA margin for the first half, and this is without any price increase 
so far in the year. As we move forward, we are optimistic of continuing similar growth and 
margin trajectory for the rest of the year. 
What gives us more confidence is that this is not a one-off. Over the last 2 years, we have been 
deliberately putting in place the foundation to sustain and accelerate this growth while 
continuing to expand margins, a denser network of centers around our labs, a richer business 
mix led by Specialty and TruHealth, standardizing our laboratory platforms, significant 
technology upgrades across business and a disciplined approach in our inorganic strategy. 
It's also worth noting that we delivered this growth in a quarter where the monsoon was one of 
the weakest in over 2 decades, with rainfall about 13% below normal and highly uneven across 
regions. The seasonal rise in acute and infectious diseases such as dengue, malaria, typhoid and 
viral fevers was therefore sporadic and varied significantly across geographies. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 19 
 
Despite this, we still grew around 16%, reinforces an important part of our business model that 
our growth is not only dependent on seasonal spikes in demand. It's also driven by the underlying 
strength of our portfolio across chronic disease management, preventive care and specialty 
testing, alongside the continued expansion of our network. 
Let me now share perspective on the industry, the regulatory environment and our strategic 
priorities. The broad picture of the industry remains consistent with what we have shared with 
you before. The market is stable and the structural shift from unorganized to organized segment 
continues, driven by a greater emphasis on quality and accuracy, rising demand for specialty 
testing, technology-led convenience and the move to preventive health care,  and wider access 
in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets. Diagnostics is not merely a price-driven business. It is a 
fundamental business driven by science, accuracy, service quality and the trust of doctors and 
patients. 
Putting in a simple way, the market is moving towards quality and science, and that's exactly 
where Metropolis has been built to compete. What is new today and what I would like to spend 
time on is the increasingly constructive role of government towards health care. Over the past 
several months, we have seen the government move to raise the bar on the diagnostics industry 
on quality, transparency and access rather than controlling price. 
Together, these developments move the industry in a direction that clearly favors organized, 
compliant players like Metropolis over unorganized, which do not necessarily focus on quality 
and service. Firstly, on price cap on pharma products for hospitals. There has been a lot of 
discussion around pricing control on drugs and consumables sold by hospitals. Let me be clear 
that this has no bearing on our business, either financially or operationally. These measures are 
aimed at hospital pricing. 
They do not extend to diagnostics, and there is no move towards price capping or price parity in 
our segment. Diagnostic pricing at organized chains is also transparent and, in most cases, 
significantly lower than comparable tests in a hospital setting. Second, the display of rates at 
centers. The requirement of display rates at centers at the point of service is a welcome change 
and one we fully support. For us, it changes very little operationally. At Metropolis, the patient 
already knows the price upfront, we collect the payment and then we deliver the service. 
In a hospital, it's usually the reverse where the service is delivered first and the patient discovers 
the bill afterwards. Mandatory display of rates brings the rest of the industry closer to the way 
we already operate. It reduces the information gap that opaque, unorganized players have relied 
on and allows patients to compare like-for-like on price and quality. When the comparison is 
transparent, we believe our accreditation, our test menu and our service standards will speak for 
themselves. 
Third is the NMC advisory on digital authorization of reports. The National Medical Council  
Commission has recently clarified that a registered medical practitioner can remotely review and 
authenticate lab and pathology reports using a recognized digital signature, subject to clear 
safeguards. This is a meaningful enabler for us in 3 ways. Number one, it improves quality. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 19 
 
Every report is reviewed by a qualified pathologist exercising independent professional 
judgment. 
Our lab information systems already maintain complete audit trails, authentication logs, 
timestamps and signing credentials on each report, thereby enabling us to target a wider network 
base for specialty testing while the talent pool resides at one location. We can now route a report 
to the right expert wherever they sit rather than relying only on whoever is on site. 
A complex hematology or oncology case from a small town can be reviewed by a specialist in 
our reference laboratory with the same rigor as a case processed in Bombay. Second, it supports 
our rural and Tier 3 expansion. One of the practical restraints in smaller towns has been the 
availability of qualified pathologists on site. 
Remote authorization allows us to set up mini labs in these markets faster with a central pool of 
pathologists supporting them while also improving turnaround times and enabling round-the-
clock reporting. Taken together, we see the evolving regulatory landscape as a clear tailwind. 
History has shown that whenever a formal regulation is introduced, business shifts more rapidly 
from unorganized to organized. We expect diagnostics to follow the same path, and we are well 
positioned not just to adapt to these changes, but to benefit from them. 
Now let's focus on our 3 key strategic priorities for growth. Science and technology remain at 
the forefront. Science has always been at the heart of Metropolis, and we continue to invest 
ahead of the curve. In genomics, we are expanding our capabilities across oncology, 
reproductive health and rare and inherited disorders. We see genomics as a significant long-term 
growth opportunity and one where scientific depth, interpretation expertise and clinician trust 
are decisive. 
We continue to invest in automation and AI across our labs and are deploying AI across the 
value chain from sample logistics and lab operations to report validation, customer engagement, 
quality improvement, TAT and productivity. 
Lastly, data protection and patient data is a responsibility we take very seriously. We are well 
advanced in aligning our systems and processes with the Digital Personal Data Protection 
Framework, which further strengthens the trust patients and doctors place in us. Let me now 
spend a moment on preventive health care, which we see also as one of the more exciting growth 
areas for our business. 
Over the past few years, preventive care has clearly moved into the mainstream. Consumers 
today are far more health conscious and proactively choosing regular checkups and early 
screenings rather than visiting a lab only when they fall ill. 
This trend is translating into strong performance for us with our preventive health care revenues 
growing at about 20% per year. To build on this momentum, we have been adding allied services 
such as basic radiology, doctor consultations and vital checks across our network in our own 
centers. This gives us a clear advantage in prescription completion because patients can now 
complete the entire set of recommended tests and consultations with us in one place under one 
trusted brand. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 19 
 
Looking ahead, we'll be piloting some new models in preventive health care in line with our 
strategy of building a strong ecosystem of allied services around our Core Diagnostics business. 
We look forward to updating you on our progress once the pilots are completed. 
Speaking of our recent acquisitions and inorganic pipeline, all the acquisitions we have done 
over the past year are performing well and integrating smoothly into the network. DAPIC in 
Dehradun and Scientific in Agra are both growing in line with the company average, while 
delivering margins higher than the overall company margins, which validates both our selection 
and our integration approach. 
Core Diagnostics is a strong example of how we create value through strategic acquisitions, 
driving both revenue growth and margin improvement. On the revenue front, the acquisition has 
strengthened our capabilities in high-end specialized testing in oncology, an area where only a 
handful of players in the country have the required expertise, while providing access to new 
clinician and patient segments. 
Importantly, cross-selling Core's specialized testing portfolio across our wider Metropolis 
network, along with upselling high-end test to our existing customer base is driving strong 
traction in the Specialty segment, which continues to grow at about 20%. At the same time, 
leveraging Core's oncology and genomics portfolio across our network has accelerated the 
growth of our own genomics business. 
On margins, Core was at breakeven when we acquired it 1.5 years ago, and today, it is delivering 
near double-digit margins. Taking into account the acceleration of our genomics business, we 
estimate that in the past year, our IRR on the Core acquisition is at about 13%, and this will only 
accelerate in H2 as revenue growth increases and margins expand. We have also completed a 
planned restructuring of the Core team. And with that now in place, our focus shifts to 
accelerating revenue further. 
Together, Core, DAPIC and Scientific have increased our revenue contribution from North India 
to about 17% of our domestic revenue, and we expect this share to rise as these businesses scale. 
Currently, the North Zone is the fastest organically growing region for us on the back of 
enhanced execution. Combined with our on-ground presence and established brand equity, these 
acquisitions have allowed us to penetrate deeper into these markets. 
We see this as a stepping stone, particularly for targeting micro markets where there is a 
persistent gap between demand and quality supply. Let me also share how we're thinking about 
the M&A market today because it shapes the deals we choose to do and the ones we choose not 
to do. 
Broadly, there are 2 kinds of businesses in the market; poor quality businesses that are up for 
sale and struggling to find buyers and some good quality businesses that have been acquired at 
very high valuations. We have looked at these deals but passed on them as it's not possible to 
earn a decent IRR. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 19 
 
The math here is important. When a diagnostics business is acquired at 18 to 20 multiple of 
EBITDA, the return depends heavily on margin expansion. But diagnostics is not like the pharma 
industry where the back end can be easily integrated and synergies flow through quickly. 
In our experience, margins in an acquired diagnostics business first fall during integration as 
quality, systems, people and processes are brought up to standard and then may recover, but 
almost never than the level higher than when they start. Therefore, at those entry multiples, the 
IRR on such deals works out to be less than 10%. 
In contrast, when we acquire businesses at reasonable valuations and then create the value 
ourselves over 3 years through our brand, test menu, specialty portfolio, logistics and 
procurement, the IRR generated can be closer to 20%. That is the approach we have followed 
with DAPIC, Scientific and Core. Looking ahead, we will continue to actively evaluate M&A 
opportunities, especially in North India across pathology and ancillary services. 
But we will prioritize deals that generate higher IRR rather than pay very high valuations just to 
buy revenue. Acquiring established local brands at the right price gives us a head start in each 
micro market from where we can expand into the surrounding peripheral markets by adding 
tests, building more organized logistics and sample movement and deepening our connect with 
doctors and patients through digital channels and tech platforms. 
I'm now going to ask Suren to go through the operational and financial performance of Q2 and 
H1. But before that, I just want to announce that the company has declared an interim dividend 
of INR1 per share. Thanks, Suren, over to you. 
Surendran Chemmenkotil: Thank you, Ameera, and good morning, everyone. Quarter 2 has been another strong quarter for 
us with revenue growth of about 16% ahead of our stated guidance. Importantly, we have seen 
healthy growth across both B2C and B2B channels, strengthened our presence in the TruHealth 
and the Specialty segments and delivered broad-based growth across all geographies, spanning 
metropolitan markets to Tier 3 and Tier 4 towns. 
This demonstrates the strength of our diversified business model and our ability to drive growth 
across channels, segments and markets. Patient volumes grew by 10% and test volume around 
11% with the balance coming from a richer test mix and better realization. 
Importantly, this growth has been delivered without any price increase. For the first half as a 
whole, revenue grew by 16.2%, a clear step-up from 12% to 13% we have delivered in recent 
years, while margin expanded by 190 bps to 26.2%, reflecting the operating leverage in our 
business. Given the consistency of this performance and the momentum we are carrying into the 
second half, we expect these trends to continue through the rest of the year. 
I would also like to address a point widely discussed in the industry in the recent past. The price 
revision in CGHS rates has supported growth for several players in the sector. Our revenue 
contribution from CGHS is minimal, so our growth has been purely volume and mix based. 
Turning into channel performance and the delivery of other segments. Our B2C revenue grew 
by 17% in quarter 2 as well as in H1 of the year, driven by sustained double-digit growth in 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 7 of 19 
 
patient and test volume, which increased by 13.5% and 11%, respectively. Patient acquisition 
was supported by digital engagement, focused micro marketing campaigns and growing brand 
across geographies and segments. 
Growth was broad-based across both mature and newer centers with existing centers delivering 
same-store growth of 10% and improved retail productivity, while newer centers continue to 
ramp up. During the quarter, we added 116 collection centers, taking our net additions to 700 
over the last 24 months. 
The labs established in financial year '25 and '26 are also gaining traction, and we are further 
strengthening their reach through an expanding network of collection spokes to drive higher 
throughput. Our B2B business grew 15%, reflecting our focused approach of partnering with 
hospitals, clinicians and quality-led institutions where our science expertise and specialty

Within B2B, patient volume grew by 7% and test volume grew by 11% which means partners 
are sending us more tests per patient, a clear sign of growing wallet share. We continue to add 
new lab and hospital partnership during the quarter, and B2B partner network has now crossed 
9,000 partners. Our partner portal continue to make it simpler for partners to work with us with 
better visibility, quicker turnaround and seamless access to our full test menu. 
On TruHealth and Specialty, both our strategic growth engines continue to deliver strong

health care franchise, also grew 20% driven by integrated wellness offerings and focused digital

We are now adding these allied services, not only in our own centers, but also across the mature 
franchisee network, which helps us improve prescription completion and offer patients complete 
health care experience under one trusted brand. 
Speaking of our performance region-wise, our growth has been broad-based geographically and 
not restricted to our core geographies. Our Tier 3 and rural centers led the way with around 20% 
revenue growth. And together, they account now for 26% of our domestic revenue, reflecting 
the success of our expansion beyond the metros. All the 4 geographical regions showed good 
growth again in this quarter, more particularly North. North India, strengthened by our 
acquisitions, now contributes to around 17% domestic revenue. 
Let me share our focus areas for the second half of the year. Accelerated center additions, both 
to cover the peripheral areas around our newer labs and to go deeper in existing markets for 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 04, 2026 
 
Page 8 of 19 
 
faster B2B partner addition with sharper focus on specialty related partnerships, mini hubs to 
bring testing closer to the patient, add basic radiology and allied services. 
And improve turnaround times, increasing retail and center productivity by getting more out of 
every existing center and of course, continued focus on Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets where 
improving access to health care is creating a large and growing base of new patients. 
Now let me speak about the margin trajectory and the improvements that we have done. 
EBITDA margins for the quarter 2 stood at 27.2%, an expansion of 180 basis points year-on-
year, well ahead of our guidance of 125 to 170 basis points. This improvement came from 
volume-led operating leverage, disciplined cost management and steady progress on our 
productivity agenda. 
What gives us confidence is that now margin expansion is sustainable as clearly visible in our 
operating metrics. Productivity per employee has improved as our manpower base has fairly 
remained stable for the last many quarters, even as test volumes grew around 10% to 11% year-
on-year. 
We are growing the business without growing the team in proportion, thereby increasing 
productivity and operating leverage. Samples processed per lab have increased per day. So each 
lab is processing higher volumes on the same fixed cost base. Gross margin improvement has 
been our prime focus. Our laboratory platform transition, which I talked earlier, standardizes our 
network on a common test menu, equipment, reagents and turnaround times while consolidating 
vendors will be completed in quarter 3, which will aid the gross margins. 
Also, richer test mix will support uptick in gross margins. We are progressively replacing many

The second half will also be a significant period for our technology transformation. We will be 
rolling out a new CRM platform, a dynamic pricing engine and new sales app for our field teams 
and an enhanced SLIMS integration capabilities across our laboratories. Through SLIMS, we 
are also working towards seamless integration of hospital portals with our systems, empowering 
our hospital partners with streamlined workflows, better connectivity and greater ease of doing

We are also transforming our finance function and have launched a comprehensive program to 
reengineer our end-to-end finance processes across all work streams. Alongside these initiatives, 
we are scaling our AI applications across customer engagement, laboratory, operations and 
quality. Together, these technology investments will make us faster, more data-driven and more 
productive while strengthening the overall experience of our customers and partners. 
Lastly, on the pricing front, our last price increase was implemented in January '25, and we are 
currently evaluating the possibility of the next price revision maybe early next year. This is being

considered in light of the increase in our operating input costs, transportation and logistic costs,

Given our strong volume trends and the structural shift towards trusted organized players, we

Our approach will be data-driven with the extent of the revision determined for each micro

time on is the increasingly constructive role of government towards health care. Over the past 
several months, we have seen the government move to raise the bar on the diagnostics industry 
on quality, transparency and access rather than controlling price.

spend a moment on preventive health care, which we see also as one of the more exciting growth

 Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 04, 2026

our hospital partners with streamlined workflows, better connectivity and greater ease of doing 
business with Metropolis. 
We are also transforming our finance function and have launched a comprehensive program to 
reengineer our end-to-end finance processes across all work streams. Alongside these initiatives, 
we are scaling our AI applications across customer engagement, laboratory, operations and 
quality. Together, these technology investments will make us faster, more data-driven and more 
productive while strengthening the overall experience of our customers and partners. 
Lastly, on the pricing front, our last price increase was implemented in January '25, and we are 
currently evaluating the possibility of the next price revision maybe early next year. This is being 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Metropolis Healthcare Limited

considered in light of the increase in our operating input costs, transportation and logistic costs, 
service costs, amongst many other expenses. 
Given our strong volume trends and the structural shift towards trusted organized players, we 
believe there is room for a calibrated price increase, enabling us to pass on a portion of these 
cost increases without any meaningful impact on volumes. 
Our approach will be data-driven with the extent of the revision determined for each micro

estimate a rollout of this in quarter 4 for part of the business. With this, I hand over the call to

on-year basis. Our focus segments continued to perform well. 
TruHealth contributed 17% of revenue and grew 20% on a year-on-year basis, while Specialty 
contributed 40% of revenue and grew 20% on a year-on-year basis. With respect to quarter 2 
margin, EBITDA stood at INR135 crores, growing 24% year-on-year. EBITDA margin 
expanded 180 basis points to 27.2%. PAT stood at INR75 crores, growing at 43% year-on-year. 
PAT margin expanded 290 basis points to 15.2%. 
This PAT margin is highest post-COVID period. On the balance sheet front, our net -- our net

that we are building. Our cash and liquid investments stood at INR348 crores as on 30th 
September 2026 compared to INR203 crores as on 31st March 2026, building a strong cash 
position to fund further our organic and inorganic growth. With this, I open the floor for question

Moderator: 
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. The first question comes from 
the line of Surya Narayan Patra, PhillipCapital India Private Limited. 
Surya Patra: 
Thanks for the opportunity and congratulations for the great set of numbers. My first question is

Surendran Chemmenkotil: So what happens for us, we count 1 TruHealth test or a wellness as 1 test. We don't count it as 8
