PRICOL Limited 
Q2 H1 FY’2027 Earnings Conference Call 
November 05, 2026 
 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the PRICOL Limited Q2 H1 FY’2027 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Valorem Advisors. 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode. There will be an opportunity 
for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need any assistance 
during this conference, please signal for an operator by pressing “*” and then “0” on your 
touchtone telephones. Please note that this conference call is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Purvangi Jain from Valorem Advisors. Thank you and 
over to you ma'am. 
Purvangi Jain: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone and a very warm welcome to you all. My name is 
Purvangi Jain from Valorem Advisors. 
We represent the investor relations of PRICOL Limited. On behalf of the company and Valorem 
Advisors, I would like to thank you all for participating in the Company's Earnings Conference 
Call for the second quarter of the financial year 2027. 
Before we begin, let me mention a short cautionary statement. Some of the statements made 
in today's earnings call may be forward-looking in nature. Such forward-looking statements are 
subject to risk and uncertainties, which could cause actual results to differ from those 
anticipated. Such statements are based on management's belief as well as assumptions made 
by and information currently available to the management. Audiences are cautioned not to 
place any undue reliance on these forward-looking statements in making any investment 
decisions. 
The purpose of today's earnings call is purely to educate and bring awareness about the 
company's fundamental business and financial quarter under review. 
I would now like to introduce you to the management team joining us on today's call. We have 
with us Mr. P.M. Ganesh – Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Mr. Siddharth 
Manoharan – Group Executive Director, Business Strategy, Ms. Madhura Mohan – Executive 
Director, Customer Relationship Management and ESG and Mr. Priyadarsi Bastia – Chief 
Financial Officer. 

Without any further delay, I request Mr. P.M. Ganesh to start with his opening remarks. Thank 
you and over to you, sir. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Purvangi. Good evening to all. Welcome to the Q2 earnings call. It is our pleasure 
in connecting with all of you once again. I am sure that you had some time to go through our 
uploaded presentation. So without any further waiting, let me go into the financial 
performance straight away. 
The Q2 financial performance, we have crossed more than a Rs. 1,000 crores in quarter 2. Rs. 
1334.02 crores has been our revenue from operations. We are at an EBITDA margin of 11.82%. 
It could have been better. If you recall in the previous earnings call, we have explained that we 
continue to face very strong headwinds, primarily because of the rising input cost. This has 
been the condition even during Q1 and it is continuing in Q2 as well. 
Primarily because of three reasons: 1) One is the strong dollar appreciation against the rupee 
and rupee has been continuously weakening. And due to the large import content in our 
product, the bill of material cost has been rising. 2) Second, as we all know that the bare PCB 
cost has been continuously increasing, which is a major ingredient in the instrument cluster. 
Primarily because of the West Asia crisis. 3) And third is the memory cost increase which has 
gone up primarily because of surge in the AI. We expect these strong headwinds to continue 
for a few more quarters before everything gets settled down. 
Coming to the PAT: 
PAT has been at Rs. 85.21 crores. The margin is at 6.39%. On H1 performance for financial year 
2027, our operation stands at Rs. 2417.60 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11.64%. The PAT 
stood at 6.30% with EPS at 12.49. 
Coming to the Quarter-on-Quarter comparison: 
Q2 for financial year 2027 when compared to the previous quarter of last financial year, the 
growth has been 35.03% in terms of revenue from operation. The EBITDA growth has been 
27.87%. On a H1 performance basis when compared to the previous year, the growth has been 
29.59% with an EBITDA growth of 24.95%. 
With this, I will hand over the mic back to Purvangi for the Q&A session. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin with the question and 
answer session. The first question is from the line of Rishabh Rathi from Goldman Sachs. Please 
go ahead. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Good evening, sir, and thank you for taking my question. My first question is around the gross 
margin impact. If you look at the gross margin, it has declined 150 bps quarter-on-quarter. But 

on the EBITDA margin, we have been able to sustain roughly similar margins. I just wanted to 
understand has some pass-through happened already or otherwise if there was no gross 
margin impact, while the plants are still ramping up, what could have been the EBITDA margin 
percentage in 2Q? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
That is what I have mentioned. The input material cost has been continuously going up because 
of the three factors, whatever I just mentioned during the opening remark. And this is expected 
to continue for at least a few quarters before it is getting normalized. And that is the reason 
why you find that the EBITDA level is lower than the growth, whatever we approach in terms 
of the top line. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Could some settlement happen in 3Q or 4Q? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Yes, actually, many of the cases we have already taken up with our customers, and customers 
are evaluating that. But as you know that there are new contents in the rising cost, primarily 
bare PCBs and memory cost and sharp increases in the labor cost. These things are something 
that the customers are evaluating because these are first-time rising costs. So you know 
customers also cannot pass on all the increases into the market. So this is currently under 
evaluation and discussion with our customers. And hopefully, we should be in a position to 
conclude it during the next quarter. But however, we expect that we would not be in a position 
to 100% recover from the customers, considering that everything the customer also cannot 
pass on to the end customer. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Right. And just for clarification, PCBs and semiconductor would not form a large part of our 
build of material right? Could the impact be somewhere around 10 bps to 20 bps, or could it 
be larger than that? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
See, I would not be in a position to give you the exact breakup detail, but bare PCBs do have a 
major content in the build-off material. I would also request that one question at a time, and 
then maybe you can join the queue for further questions, please. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Got it. Thank you.  
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Hitesh Goyal from Origin Capital. Please go 
ahead. 
Hitesh Goyal: 
Thanks for taking my question. Sir, can you give us the growth rates in the DIS business, ACFMS 
and plastic business separately in this quarter? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
We have overall, Hitesh, grown by 35%, okay? And all the three divisions have seen more or 
less the same level of growth. So that is why you find when compared to the previous year, 
quarter 2, we have grown by 35%. 

Hitesh Goyal: 
Okay. So no segment has grown? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
All our vertical has grown actually at the same rate, whatever I mentioned to you. 
Hitesh Goyal: 
And sir, you said that, just for clarification, you said that next quarter also you will see the 
headwinds, you can see that. But are you saying that gross margin could deteriorate further in 
the next quarter? We will see at this 11%, 12% kind of EBITDA range? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
It is a little difficult for us to predict because the cost has been continuously raising, Hitesh, 
number one. Second thing is, many of the increases, whatever has happened, we have already 
taken up with the customers for concluding it. We are not very sure at this point of time how 
it will turn out. 
Hitesh Goyal: 
Got it, sir. No problem. Thank you very much and all the best. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Hitesh. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of A. Sriram from ithought PMS. Please go ahead. 
A. Sriram: 
Sir, within ACFMS, can you mention which is the top driver within ACFMS? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
The ACFMS division, the top driver comes from the fuel pump, whatever we supply to two-
wheeler application. We are one of the largest in the country to make the fuel pumps for two-
wheeler application. And the second is coming from various export customers. As we 
mentioned in the previous earning call, Caterpillar is one of our largest customers in the U.S. 
where we export to the larger water pumps. So it is the combination of the fuel pump business 
for domestic and also export customers for the large pumps. 
A. Sriram: 
Thank you, sir. I will come back in queue. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Sriram. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Sahil Sanghvi from Monarch Network Capital. 
Please go ahead. 
Sahil Sanghvi: 
Hi, sir. Huge congratulations for an excellent set of performance. I just wanted some more 
understanding on what are the reasons for the kind of growth we have done this quarter. I 
mean, even if we compare it to the underlying industry growth and we account for some 
premiumization, there was a beat all around. And this being, considering that we have 
previously said that we are limited on capacities for the plastic business. So if you can help us, 
was there new model additions? Was there something else on the products? How we have 
been able to achieve this kind of growth and how sustainable is this number? 

P.M. Ganesh: 
Sahil, thanks for your question. The growth primarily has been driven by strong domestic 
demand. And you would have seen coupled with the festive season, the demand has been very, 
very robust. And you would have seen two-wheeler has recorded the highest growth ever in 
the history of two-wheeler at 35%. And we have grown with the two-wheeler segment. And 
two-wheeler business is our large forte. This is number one. Second thing is you would have 
seen that some new product launches have happened during Q2. In the presentation, whatever 
we have uploaded, primarily the Bajaj Pulsar, which we have launched with our new TFT, new 
generation TFT clusters, which also has given good amount of value addition to the product. So 
a combination of this actually has helped us to grow in Q2 when compared to the previous 
quarter. 
Sahil Sanghvi: 
Thank you, sir. I will come back in the queue. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Preet Pitani from Incred AMC. Please go ahead. 
Preet Pitani: 
Thank you for the opportunity, sir. My question is on the line of raw material cost. You 
mentioned that we are not able to get complete pass-on of the raw material cost inflation 
which has happened. So during the times of deflationary raw material, do we need to pass on 
complete raw material cost deflation? Or at that time also it happens in the same way? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
See, Preet, it is something like this. See, we have indexed with our customer as pass-through 
both on the raw material and FOREX. That is happening on a quarterly basis very regularly and 
systematically. But starting from the West Asia crisis, there has been some abnormal increase, 
which it is first time for the customer also. Like what I mentioned, the bare PCB cost swelling 
up, and then the memory cost going up significantly because of the AI disruption, and then also 
many of the input material cost going up because of the casting, machining, and sharp increase 
in labor cost because of the GO incorporated at the northern part of India. These are something 
first time the customer also is there, so of course with the industry. We are not very sure. We 
have put up all these cost increases to the customer, but we are not very sure that how much 
would be recovered from the customer at this point of time. It is currently under discussion. 
That is why I said we are not very sure whether we will be in a position to recover 100% on 
these one first time cost, whatever has happened since Q1. 
Preet Pitani: 
How much will be the impact on the cost on our Q2 numbers? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
It is very difficult for me to define and tell you what is the percentage because product to 
product it will change. 
Preet Pitani: 
Blanket dump range, it will be the north of 50 to 60 basis point or higher than that? 

P.M. Ganesh: 
At least on an EBITDA level, it should be 1% to 2% in my opinion. I am just giving you a rough 
number. It should be 1% to 2% in terms of the first-time cost escalations, whatever has 
happened ever since Q1. 
Preet Pitani: 
If we get a complete pass through, our EBITDA margin would be in the range of 12.5% to 13%. 
Is my understanding correct? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
I cannot put A plus B is equal to C. That is why I am telling product to product it differs. If I go 
to an ACFMS product, there is no major import content whereas the labour cost has gone up. 
If I go to DICVS product, then you have the memory disruption and the bare PCB. So these 
combinational effects actually, that is why I am not able to put A number to that. So I am just 
giving a guesstimated number to you for your understanding. 
Preet Pitani: 
Got it sir. That was very much helpful. Thank you. I will join back in the queue. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Rishabh Rathi from Goldman Sachs. Please go 
ahead. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Thank you sir. Just one follow up question on the plastics business. You talked about adding 
capacity and commercializing it somewhere around the second half. Can you help us 
understand what was like the full year revenue last year in the plastic business and the rough 
range of what we are expecting this year in FY’28 based on the capacity and production, etc? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
I will request this question to be taken by our Group Executive Director, Siddharth. Over to you, 
Siddharth. 
Siddharth Manoharan: 
Thank you, sir. So, to answer your question on all the CAPEX items, so last year we have clocked 
close to 950 to 1000 top line, and we are also seeing a good amount of growth. I would not be 
able to make statements on the value for closing the year, but the pipeline of business is good, 
and we have also won sizable new businesses from various other OEMs as well. But as we 
mentioned in the last earnings call, right now our focus is on creating the capacity. We are 
almost operating at 100% capacity. So with the budgeted CAPEX announced, so next 12 months 
is going to be the time frame for us to create all the capacities and then put them into 
operations. And the real growth of the business will happen from FY’28 and thereupon. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Got it. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of A. Sriram from ithought PMS. Please go ahead. 
A. Sriram: 
In the last earnings call, you mentioned the customers of polymer business. So may I know who 
are the major customers among them? 

Siddharth Manoharan: 
So our top key customers are TVS, Ather Energy, Royal Enfield, Autoliv, and we have also won 
sizable business with Honda Motorcycles who will also become a key customer in the upcoming 
financial year. 
A. Sriram: 
Thank you sir. 
Siddharth Manoharan: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Nandan Pradhan from Emkay Global. Please 
go ahead. 
Nandan Pradhan: 
Good afternoon team and congratulations on a great set of numbers in such a volatile 
environment. Sir, just a small bookkeeping question if you may help us with the performance 
for P3L in this quarter. We have been maintaining that in the quarter. Help us with that. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Nandan, your question is not very audible to us. Can you just repeat your question, please? 
Nandan Pradhan: 
Yes. Is this better? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Yes, that is better, Nandan. 
Nandan Pradhan: 
Yes. So I just wanted to understand the performance of P3L for this quarter specifically. Just 
the revenue and EBITDA, if you could help us with the same. 
Siddharth Manoharan: 
Priyan, would you like to take or should I go ahead? 
Priyadarsi Bastia: 
Yes. I am answering, Siddharth. Nandan, for Q2, revenue for P3L stands at Rs. 312 crores with 
9.9% of EBITDA. Thank you. 
Nandan Pradhan: 
Thank you so much, sir. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Nandan. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Jatin Chawla from RCL Investments. Please go 
ahead. 
Jatin Chawla: 
Yes, hi. Good afternoon and thanks for the opportunity. My first question is, I think last quarter 
you had spoken about winning a lot of business with Honda on the DIS side as well. Has that 
started scaling up already or when should we expect those kind of numbers to come through? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Jatin, actually it was not during last earnings call. It was a year back that we have already 
entered into Honda business on the electronic LCD clusters and we have been continuously 

growing Honda business. So it is actually nothing new during the last quarter. We have been in 
a very sustainable and growing business with Honda for the last couple of years. 
Jatin Chawla: 
Got it. So it was on the plastic side where you will see some more kind of acceleration going 
forward. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
That is right.  
Jatin Chawla: 
My question was on, you know, the pass-through that happens on a quarterly basis. I think 
what we are seeing is 2Q there was inflation and hence whatever pass-through you would have 
got is not visible. Does it start becoming from 3Q onwards or it is only in 4Q where we start 
seeing some benefit on that? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
See, that is what I explained to you, Jatin, that Q1 onwards there has been abnormal increase 
in terms of the input material cost. Okay. It is just not FOREX and raw material. But there has 
been electronic component increase, whatever I explained to you. So what is happening is it is 
continuously going up. So whatever we do as a pass-through with customer in the previous 
understanding, we are able to recover. Okay. But there are new first-time increases which has 
happened since Q1. Like what I explained to you, the bare PCBs, memory, labor cost increases, 
power cost increases going up in the casting side. So these are the first time such kind of sharp 
increases has happened in the industry. These we have already put up with the customer and 
this is under negotiation. 
Jatin Chawla: 
Got it. Thanks a lot. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Jatin. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Vipul Kumar from Sumangal Investments. 
Please go ahead. 
Vipul Kumar: 
Hi. Thanks for the opportunity. So what is the CAPEX for increasing the capacity for this plastic 
division? And what will be the asset turn for that? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
I will request our CFO Priyan to answer this question, please. 
Priyadarsi Bastia: 
Vipul, as explained in the earlier earnings call, for this financial year, rather next six quarters, 
our CAPEX will be Rs.350 crores in that entity, P3L. And the asset turn will be around 3. 
Vipul Kumar: 
Would you repeat please? Asset turn? 
Priyadarsi Bastia: 
Asset turn will be around 3 to 3.25. 
Vipul Kumar: 
Thank you. 

Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Preet Pitani from Incred AMC. Please go ahead. 
Preet Pitani: 
Thank you for the follow-up opportunity, sir. My question is on the line of growth drivers. 
Industry production growth was around 20% for second quarter and we have grown at 35%. 
And as you mentioned to the previous participants, that we have grown 35% in both the 
segments, DIC as well as ACFMS. So what would be the additional growth driver apart from 
content addition? Would it be market share gain? If you could just brief that. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Yes, actually, if you see the overall market, I agree with you, it has grown by 20%. But however, 
two-wheeler in particular has grown by around 35% during Q2 of the same period during last 
year and compared to the last year. And you know, a significant portion of our sale comes from 
the two-wheeler segment. That has really helped us, number one. Second thing is, of course, 
the value-added products have kicked in. Bajaj example, which I gave it to you, second. And 
third, actually, the value-added ACFMS products like the fuel pump and the heavy-duty water 
pump, whatever we are exporting to U.S, has really grown during this quarter. And that is the 
reason why you find that we are above the market in terms of the growth. 
Preet Pitani: 
And in terms of market share, have we lost or gained any market share? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
I think market share, definitely we have not lost. And we have gained some market share 
because of the new product, whatever we have launched during Q2, both on the driver 
information system and also on the plastics and also on the ACFMS. 
Preet Pitani: 
Got it, sir. I will join back in the queue. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Chandra Gupta from the Long Castle Capital 
Management. Please go ahead. 
Chandra Gupta: 
Hello. Am I audible? 
Moderator: 
Yes, sir, you are. 
Chandra Gupta: 
Sir, my question is about the demerger. Can you just update us on where we stand now? What 
are the timelines that you are looking at when the proposal will be filed with NCLT. And also, 
last time it was mentioned that from 1st October, we will be internally operating as two 
separate companies. So whether that has happened? Can you update us on this? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Yes, this question I will ask our Group Executive Director Mr. Siddharth to answer, please. 
Siddharth Manoharan: 
Yes. Mr. Chandra Gupta, so the demerger process is ongoing. So we have submitted our 
application and going through the motions of it at this point in time. It is expected to take a 

couple of quarters until the final orders are being given to us. Internally, as you rightly 
mentioned, from October onwards, we have started operationalizing, divisionalizing of the 
company. So certain internal controls have been put in, people have been moved. So that 
process has been started and we expect it to go forward for the next six months. From 1st April, 
2027 onwards, we plan to operationalize the company completely into two different divisions, 
which is DICVS and ACFMS divisions. 
Chandra Gupta: 
Okay. Okay. Thanks a lot. That is all from my side. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, we take that as the last question. I now hand the floor over 
to the management for closing comments. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
 Thank you, Purvangi. I will request our CFO, Priyan, for the closing remarks. 
Priyadarsi Bastia: 
Thank you, ladies and gentlemen. We remain deeply focused on executing our long-term 
visions, long-term goals. And thank you for joining us today. We look forward to updating you 
on our next progress in the next quarter call. Thank you so much. Happy Diwali to all. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much, sir. On behalf of PRICOL Limited, that concludes this conference call. 
Thank you all for joining and you may now disconnect your lines. Thank you.

PRICOL Limited 
Q2 H1 FY’2027 Earnings Conference Call 
November 05, 2026 
 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the PRICOL Limited Q2 H1 FY’2027 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Valorem Advisors. 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode. There will be an opportunity 
for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need any assistance 
during this conference, please signal for an operator by pressing “*” and then “0” on your 
touchtone telephones. Please note that this conference call is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Purvangi Jain from Valorem Advisors. Thank you and 
over to you ma'am. 
Purvangi Jain: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone and a very warm welcome to you all. My name is 
Purvangi Jain from Valorem Advisors. 
We represent the investor relations of PRICOL Limited. On behalf of the company and Valorem 
Advisors, I would like to thank you all for participating in the Company's Earnings Conference 
Call for the second quarter of the financial year 2027. 
Before we begin, let me mention a short cautionary statement. Some of the statements made 
in today's earnings call may be forward-looking in nature. Such forward-looking statements are 
subject to risk and uncertainties, which could cause actual results to differ from those 
anticipated. Such statements are based on management's belief as well as assumptions made 
by and information currently available to the management. Audiences are cautioned not to 
place any undue reliance on these forward-looking statements in making any investment 
decisions. 
The purpose of today's earnings call is purely to educate and bring awareness about the 
company's fundamental business and financial quarter under review. 
I would now like to introduce you to the management team joining us on today's call. We have 
with us Mr. P.M. Ganesh – Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Mr. Siddharth 
Manoharan – Group Executive Director, Business Strategy, Ms. Madhura Mohan – Executive 
Director, Customer Relationship Management and ESG and Mr. Priyadarsi Bastia – Chief 
Financial Officer. 

Without any further delay, I request Mr. P.M. Ganesh to start with his opening remarks. Thank 
you and over to you, sir. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Purvangi. Good evening to all. Welcome to the Q2 earnings call. It is our pleasure 
in connecting with all of you once again. I am sure that you had some time to go through our 
uploaded presentation. So without any further waiting, let me go into the financial 
performance straight away. 
The Q2 financial performance, we have crossed more than a Rs. 1,000 crores in quarter 2. Rs. 
1334.02 crores has been our revenue from operations. We are at an EBITDA margin of 11.82%. 
It could have been better. If you recall in the previous earnings call, we have explained that we 
continue to face very strong headwinds, primarily because of the rising input cost. This has 
been the condition even during Q1 and it is continuing in Q2 as well. 
Primarily because of three reasons: 1) One is the strong dollar appreciation against the rupee 
and rupee has been continuously weakening. And due to the large import content in our 
product, the bill of material cost has been rising. 2) Second, as we all know that the bare PCB 
cost has been continuously increasing, which is a major ingredient in the instrument cluster. 
Primarily because of the West Asia crisis. 3) And third is the memory cost increase which has 
gone up primarily because of surge in the AI. We expect these strong headwinds to continue 
for a few more quarters before everything gets settled down. 
Coming to the PAT: 
PAT has been at Rs. 85.21 crores. The margin is at 6.39%. On H1 performance for financial year 
2027, our operation stands at Rs. 2417.60 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11.64%. The PAT 
stood at 6.30% with EPS at 12.49. 
Coming to the Quarter-on-Quarter comparison: 
Q2 for financial year 2027 when compared to the previous quarter of last financial year, the 
growth has been 35.03% in terms of revenue from operation. The EBITDA growth has been 
27.87%. On a H1 performance basis when compared to the previous year, the growth has been 
29.59% with an EBITDA growth of 24.95%. 
With this, I will hand over the mic back to Purvangi for the Q&A session. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin with the question and 
answer session. The first question is from the line of Rishabh Rathi from Goldman Sachs. Please 
go ahead. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Good evening, sir, and thank you for taking my question. My first question is around the gross 
margin impact. If you look at the gross margin, it has declined 150 bps quarter-on-quarter. But 

on the EBITDA margin, we have been able to sustain roughly similar margins. I just wanted to 
understand has some pass-through happened already or otherwise if there was no gross 
margin impact, while the plants are still ramping up, what could have been the EBITDA margin 
percentage in 2Q? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
That is what I have mentioned. The input material cost has been continuously going up because 
of the three factors, whatever I just mentioned during the opening remark. And this is expected 
to continue for at least a few quarters before it is getting normalized. And that is the reason 
why you find that the EBITDA level is lower than the growth, whatever we approach in terms 
of the top line. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Could some settlement happen in 3Q or 4Q? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Yes, actually, many of the cases we have already taken up with our customers, and customers 
are evaluating that. But as you know that there are new contents in the rising cost, primarily 
bare PCBs and memory cost and sharp increases in the labor cost. These things are something 
that the customers are evaluating because these are first-time rising costs. So you know 
customers also cannot pass on all the increases into the market. So this is currently under 
evaluation and discussion with our customers. And hopefully, we should be in a position to 
conclude it during the next quarter. But however, we expect that we would not be in a position 
to 100% recover from the customers, considering that everything the customer also cannot 
pass on to the end customer. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Right. And just for clarification, PCBs and semiconductor would not form a large part of our 
build of material right? Could the impact be somewhere around 10 bps to 20 bps, or could it 
be larger than that? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
See, I would not be in a position to give you the exact breakup detail, but bare PCBs do have a 
major content in the build-off material. I would also request that one question at a time, and 
then maybe you can join the queue for further questions, please. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Got it. Thank you.  
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Hitesh Goyal from Origin Capital. Please go 
ahead. 
Hitesh Goyal: 
Thanks for taking my question. Sir, can you give us the growth rates in the DIS business, ACFMS 
and plastic business separately in this quarter? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
We have overall, Hitesh, grown by 35%, okay? And all the three divisions have seen more or 
less the same level of growth. So that is why you find when compared to the previous year, 
quarter 2, we have grown by 35%. 

Hitesh Goyal: 
Okay. So no segment has grown? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
All our vertical has grown actually at the same rate, whatever I mentioned to you. 
Hitesh Goyal: 
And sir, you said that, just for clarification, you said that next quarter also you will see the 
headwinds, you can see that. But are you saying that gross margin could deteriorate further in 
the next quarter? We will see at this 11%, 12% kind of EBITDA range? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
It is a little difficult for us to predict because the cost has been continuously raising, Hitesh, 
number one. Second thing is, many of the increases, whatever has happened, we have already 
taken up with the customers for concluding it. We are not very sure at this point of time how 
it will turn out. 
Hitesh Goyal: 
Got it, sir. No problem. Thank you very much and all the best. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Hitesh. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of A. Sriram from ithought PMS. Please go ahead. 
A. Sriram: 
Sir, within ACFMS, can you mention which is the top driver within ACFMS? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
The ACFMS division, the top driver comes from the fuel pump, whatever we supply to two-
wheeler application. We are one of the largest in the country to make the fuel pumps for two-
wheeler application. And the second is coming from various export customers. As we 
mentioned in the previous earning call, Caterpillar is one of our largest customers in the U.S. 
where we export to the larger water pumps. So it is the combination of the fuel pump business 
for domestic and also export customers for the large pumps. 
A. Sriram: 
Thank you, sir. I will come back in queue. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Sriram. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Sahil Sanghvi from Monarch Network Capital. 
Please go ahead. 
Sahil Sanghvi: 
Hi, sir. Huge congratulations for an excellent set of performance. I just wanted some more 
understanding on what are the reasons for the kind of growth we have done this quarter. I 
mean, even if we compare it to the underlying industry growth and we account for some 
premiumization, there was a beat all around. And this being, considering that we have 
previously said that we are limited on capacities for the plastic business. So if you can help us, 
was there new model additions? Was there something else on the products? How we have 
been able to achieve this kind of growth and how sustainable is this number? 

P.M. Ganesh: 
Sahil, thanks for your question. The growth primarily has been driven by strong domestic 
demand. And you would have seen coupled with the festive season, the demand has been very, 
very robust. And you would have seen two-wheeler has recorded the highest growth ever in 
the history of two-wheeler at 35%. And we have grown with the two-wheeler segment. And 
two-wheeler business is our large forte. This is number one. Second thing is you would have 
seen that some new product launches have happened during Q2. In the presentation, whatever 
we have uploaded, primarily the Bajaj Pulsar, which we have launched with our new TFT, new 
generation TFT clusters, which also has given good amount of value addition to the product. So 
a combination of this actually has helped us to grow in Q2 when compared to the previous 
quarter. 
Sahil Sanghvi: 
Thank you, sir. I will come back in the queue. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Preet Pitani from Incred AMC. Please go ahead. 
Preet Pitani: 
Thank you for the opportunity, sir. My question is on the line of raw material cost. You 
mentioned that we are not able to get complete pass-on of the raw material cost inflation 
which has happened. So during the times of deflationary raw material, do we need to pass on 
complete raw material cost deflation? Or at that time also it happens in the same way? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
See, Preet, it is something like this. See, we have indexed with our customer as pass-through 
both on the raw material and FOREX. That is happening on a quarterly basis very regularly and 
systematically. But starting from the West Asia crisis, there has been some abnormal increase, 
which it is first time for the customer also. Like what I mentioned, the bare PCB cost swelling 
up, and then the memory cost going up significantly because of the AI disruption, and then also 
many of the input material cost going up because of the casting, machining, and sharp increase 
in labor cost because of the GO incorporated at the northern part of India. These are something 
first time the customer also is there, so of course with the industry. We are not very sure. We 
have put up all these cost increases to the customer, but we are not very sure that how much 
would be recovered from the customer at this point of time. It is currently under discussion. 
That is why I said we are not very sure whether we will be in a position to recover 100% on 
these one first time cost, whatever has happened since Q1. 
Preet Pitani: 
How much will be the impact on the cost on our Q2 numbers? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
It is very difficult for me to define and tell you what is the percentage because product to 
product it will change. 
Preet Pitani: 
Blanket dump range, it will be the north of 50 to 60 basis point or higher than that? 

P.M. Ganesh: 
At least on an EBITDA level, it should be 1% to 2% in my opinion. I am just giving you a rough 
number. It should be 1% to 2% in terms of the first-time cost escalations, whatever has 
happened ever since Q1. 
Preet Pitani: 
If we get a complete pass through, our EBITDA margin would be in the range of 12.5% to 13%. 
Is my understanding correct? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
I cannot put A plus B is equal to C. That is why I am telling product to product it differs. If I go 
to an ACFMS product, there is no major import content whereas the labour cost has gone up. 
If I go to DICVS product, then you have the memory disruption and the bare PCB. So these 
combinational effects actually, that is why I am not able to put A number to that. So I am just 
giving a guesstimated number to you for your understanding. 
Preet Pitani: 
Got it sir. That was very much helpful. Thank you. I will join back in the queue. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Rishabh Rathi from Goldman Sachs. Please go 
ahead. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Thank you sir. Just one follow up question on the plastics business. You talked about adding 
capacity and commercializing it somewhere around the second half. Can you help us 
understand what was like the full year revenue last year in the plastic business and the rough 
range of what we are expecting this year in FY’28 based on the capacity and production, etc? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
I will request this question to be taken by our Group Executive Director, Siddharth. Over to you, 
Siddharth. 
Siddharth Manoharan: 
Thank you, sir. So, to answer your question on all the CAPEX items, so last year we have clocked 
close to 950 to 1000 top line, and we are also seeing a good amount of growth. I would not be 
able to make statements on the value for closing the year, but the pipeline of business is good, 
and we have also won sizable new businesses from various other OEMs as well. But as we 
mentioned in the last earnings call, right now our focus is on creating the capacity. We are 
almost operating at 100% capacity. So with the budgeted CAPEX announced, so next 12 months 
is going to be the time frame for us to create all the capacities and then put them into 
operations. And the real growth of the business will happen from FY’28 and thereupon. 
Rishabh Rathi: 
Got it. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of A. Sriram from ithought PMS. Please go ahead. 
A. Sriram: 
In the last earnings call, you mentioned the customers of polymer business. So may I know who 
are the major customers among them? 

Siddharth Manoharan: 
So our top key customers are TVS, Ather Energy, Royal Enfield, Autoliv, and we have also won 
sizable business with Honda Motorcycles who will also become a key customer in the upcoming 
financial year. 
A. Sriram: 
Thank you sir. 
Siddharth Manoharan: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Nandan Pradhan from Emkay Global. Please 
go ahead. 
Nandan Pradhan: 
Good afternoon team and congratulations on a great set of numbers in such a volatile 
environment. Sir, just a small bookkeeping question if you may help us with the performance 
for P3L in this quarter. We have been maintaining that in the quarter. Help us with that. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Nandan, your question is not very audible to us. Can you just repeat your question, please? 
Nandan Pradhan: 
Yes. Is this better? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Yes, that is better, Nandan. 
Nandan Pradhan: 
Yes. So I just wanted to understand the performance of P3L for this quarter specifically. Just 
the revenue and EBITDA, if you could help us with the same. 
Siddharth Manoharan: 
Priyan, would you like to take or should I go ahead? 
Priyadarsi Bastia: 
Yes. I am answering, Siddharth. Nandan, for Q2, revenue for P3L stands at Rs. 312 crores with 
9.9% of EBITDA. Thank you. 
Nandan Pradhan: 
Thank you so much, sir. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Nandan. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Jatin Chawla from RCL Investments. Please go 
ahead. 
Jatin Chawla: 
Yes, hi. Good afternoon and thanks for the opportunity. My first question is, I think last quarter 
you had spoken about winning a lot of business with Honda on the DIS side as well. Has that 
started scaling up already or when should we expect those kind of numbers to come through? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Jatin, actually it was not during last earnings call. It was a year back that we have already 
entered into Honda business on the electronic LCD clusters and we have been continuously 

growing Honda business. So it is actually nothing new during the last quarter. We have been in 
a very sustainable and growing business with Honda for the last couple of years. 
Jatin Chawla: 
Got it. So it was on the plastic side where you will see some more kind of acceleration going 
forward. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
That is right.  
Jatin Chawla: 
My question was on, you know, the pass-through that happens on a quarterly basis. I think 
what we are seeing is 2Q there was inflation and hence whatever pass-through you would have 
got is not visible. Does it start becoming from 3Q onwards or it is only in 4Q where we start 
seeing some benefit on that? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
See, that is what I explained to you, Jatin, that Q1 onwards there has been abnormal increase 
in terms of the input material cost. Okay. It is just not FOREX and raw material. But there has 
been electronic component increase, whatever I explained to you. So what is happening is it is 
continuously going up. So whatever we do as a pass-through with customer in the previous 
understanding, we are able to recover. Okay. But there are new first-time increases which has 
happened since Q1. Like what I explained to you, the bare PCBs, memory, labor cost increases, 
power cost increases going up in the casting side. So these are the first time such kind of sharp 
increases has happened in the industry. These we have already put up with the customer and 
this is under negotiation. 
Jatin Chawla: 
Got it. Thanks a lot. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you, Jatin. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Vipul Kumar from Sumangal Investments. 
Please go ahead. 
Vipul Kumar: 
Hi. Thanks for the opportunity. So what is the CAPEX for increasing the capacity for this plastic 
division? And what will be the asset turn for that? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
I will request our CFO Priyan to answer this question, please. 
Priyadarsi Bastia: 
Vipul, as explained in the earlier earnings call, for this financial year, rather next six quarters, 
our CAPEX will be Rs.350 crores in that entity, P3L. And the asset turn will be around 3. 
Vipul Kumar: 
Would you repeat please? Asset turn? 
Priyadarsi Bastia: 
Asset turn will be around 3 to 3.25. 
Vipul Kumar: 
Thank you. 

Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Preet Pitani from Incred AMC. Please go ahead. 
Preet Pitani: 
Thank you for the follow-up opportunity, sir. My question is on the line of growth drivers. 
Industry production growth was around 20% for second quarter and we have grown at 35%. 
And as you mentioned to the previous participants, that we have grown 35% in both the 
segments, DIC as well as ACFMS. So what would be the additional growth driver apart from 
content addition? Would it be market share gain? If you could just brief that. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Yes, actually, if you see the overall market, I agree with you, it has grown by 20%. But however, 
two-wheeler in particular has grown by around 35% during Q2 of the same period during last 
year and compared to the last year. And you know, a significant portion of our sale comes from 
the two-wheeler segment. That has really helped us, number one. Second thing is, of course, 
the value-added products have kicked in. Bajaj example, which I gave it to you, second. And 
third, actually, the value-added ACFMS products like the fuel pump and the heavy-duty water 
pump, whatever we are exporting to U.S, has really grown during this quarter. And that is the 
reason why you find that we are above the market in terms of the growth. 
Preet Pitani: 
And in terms of market share, have we lost or gained any market share? 
P.M. Ganesh: 
I think market share, definitely we have not lost. And we have gained some market share 
because of the new product, whatever we have launched during Q2, both on the driver 
information system and also on the plastics and also on the ACFMS. 
Preet Pitani: 
Got it, sir. I will join back in the queue. 
P.M. Ganesh: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Chandra Gupta from the Long Castle Capital 
Management. Please go ahead. 
Chandra Gupta: 
Hello. Am I audible? 
Moderator: 
Yes, sir, you are. 
Chandra Gupta: 
Sir, my question is about the demerger. Can you just update us on where we stand now? What 
are the timelines that you are looking at when the proposal will be filed with NCLT. And also,

P.M. Ganesh: 
Yes, this question I will ask our Group Executive Director Mr. Siddharth to answer, please. 
Siddharth Manoharan: 
Yes. Mr. Chandra Gupta, so the demerger process is ongoing. So we have submitted our 
application and going through the motions of it at this point in time. It is expected to take a 

couple of quarters until the final orders are being given to us. Internally, as you rightly 
mentioned, from October onwards, we have started operationalizing, divisionalizing of the 
company. So certain internal controls have been put in, people have been moved. So that 
process has been started and we expect it to go forward for the next six months. From 1st April, 
2027 onwards, we plan to operationalize the company completely into two different divisions,

Chandra Gupta: 
Okay. Okay. Thanks a lot. That is all from my side.

 Thank you, Purvangi. I will request our CFO, Priyan, for the closing remarks.

Q2 & H1FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
Nov 05, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Management: 
Mr. K.A. Joseph – Managing Director & Promoter

Ms. Devanshi Dhruva – Head – Investor Relations 
 
Analyst: 
 
Mr. Jay Kale – Elara Capital 
 

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to SJS Enterprises Limited Q2 FY 2027 Earnings 
Conference Call. 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing “*” then “0” on your touch-
tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Jay Kale from Elara Capital. Thank you, and over to you, 
Sir. 
Jay Kale: 
Thank you, and good morning, everyone, and Season's Greetings to all. 
On behalf of Elara Capital, I welcome you to the Q2 FY 2027 Earnings Conference Call of SJS 
Enterprises Limited. From the Management Team, we have with us today Mr. K. A. Joseph – 
Promoter and Managing Director; Mr. Sanjay Thapar – Group CEO and Executive Director; Mr. 
Mahendra Naredi – Group CFO; and Ms. Devanshi Dhruva – Head Investor Relations. 
I would now hand over the call to Ms. Devanshi Dhruva for her opening remarks. Over to you. 
Devanshi Dhruva: 
Thank you, Jay, and good morning, ladies and gentlemen. We appreciate you joining us on 
today's Conference Call. 
We will begin the call with opening remarks from Mr. K. A. Joseph – our Managing Director, 
followed by a business and industry overview from Mr. Sanjay Thapar – our Group CEO and 
Executive Director. After that, Mr. Mahendra Naredi – our Group CFO, will walk us through 
the financial performance for the quarter.  
We will then open the floor for questions. Please note that the duration of this call is expected 
to be around 60 minutes, with the first 20 minutes reserved for our prepared comments. Should 
there be enough time for all questions, please feel free to reach out to us via email, and we will 
respond to your inquiries at the earliest. 
Thank you once again for your time today and with that, I will now hand it over to Mr. Joseph 
for his opening remarks. Over to you, Joseph sir. 
K. A. Joseph: 
Yes. Thank you, Devanshi, and good morning, everyone. I trust you all had an opportunity to 
review our Investor Presentation and the Financial Results for the 2nd quarter and the first half 
of FY 2027. 
India's automotive industry grew production volumes by 17.8% in Q2FY2027, led by passenger 
vehicles at 24.9% and two-wheelers at 16.5%. Premiumization and the growing adoption of 
advanced features continue to expand our content per vehicle opportunity. In Q2 FY 2027, SJS 

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
witnessed a steady growth of 21.7% YoY in automotive driven by premium products, higher 
content per vehicle, and deeper OEM relationships. Consolidated revenue rose by 16.9% YoY 
to Rs. 2,827.3 million, led by robust growth in passenger vehicle and exports. H1FY2027 
revenue grew by 20.4% to Rs. 5,437.3 million. PAT for the quarter stood at Rs. 583.3 million, 
with a margin of 20.6%, highest since our IPO. H1FY2027 reported PAT of Rs. 1,327.5 million. 
Higher exports, favorable product mix, and operational efficiency remain central to sustaining 
profitability as we scale. 
On the capacity expansion front, our new SJS Decoplast chrome plating facility in Pune 
commenced operations in August of 2026, and the Bangalore plant expansion is also complete, 
with commercial production starting in Q3 of FY2027. Further, the consolidation of Walter 
Pack's three Ranjangaon facilities into a single integrated larger plant will drive operational 
efficiency and support future growth. With a net cash of Rs. 3,318.7 million at the end of 
September 2026, we have the flexibility to fund capex, strategic initiatives, and potential 
acquisitions. 
Going forward, we remain focused on innovation, premium products, and international 
expansion. Our design and R&D strengths, customer relationships with new program pipeline 
positions SJS well for profitable growth. 
Now, I hand over to Sanjay for the business and industry highlights. Over to you, Sanjay. 
Sanjay Thapar: 
Thank you, Joe, and good morning, everyone. We concluded the first half of FY2027 with steady 
progress on both financial performance and strategic priorities. Our focus on premiumization, 
deeper customer relationships, and investments in technology and capacity continue to create 
new business opportunities, increasing our content per vehicle and widening our presence across 
automotive and consumer applications. 
Let me take you through the key updates for the quarter and half year: 
In Q2FY2027, consolidated revenue grew 16.9% year-on-year to Rs. 282.73 crore, driven by 
passenger vehicles and a rising contribution from exports. Our automotive business grew 21.7% 
against industry production growth of 17.8%. Our ability to supply multiple aesthetic products 
across customer platforms continues to drive growth ahead of industry volumes. Uncertain 
macros, prolonged geopolitical conflicts, and a planned rationalization of low-margin SKUs 
with Walter Pack India Consumer OEM softened the consumer segment performance, partly 
offsetting strong growth in the automotive and export segments. 
Further, two-wheeler growth was led by scooters, 30.1% year-on-year growth for Q2 over 
motorcycles, which was 9.8% year-on-year growth, which is the core SJS segment that we focus 
on, a gap that has widened significantly this year. SJS Automotive business grew 21.7% against 
a 13.2% industry growth for passenger vehicles and motorcycles combined, indicating an 

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
outperformance by SJS and continued share gains even as scooters, where SJS has limited 
presence, outpaced motorcycles. EBITDA rose 23.1% year-on-year to Rs. 896.4 million, with a 
margin of 31%, supported by better product mix, higher exports, and operating efficiency. 
Despite moderate revenue growth, EBITDA has continued its steady upward trajectory, 
reflecting the strength of our margin profile and disciplined execution. PAT grew 34.8% to Rs. 
583.3 million, with a margin of 20.6%. On the capacity front, new chrome plating facility at SJS 
Decoplast in Pune commenced operations in August 2026, adding 2x capacity and flexibility for 
new customer programs and emerging opportunities. Our Bengaluru facility expansion is 
complete with a 20% capacity addition and commercial production likely to start in Q3. 
SJS Display Electronics Private Limited is setting up an automotive display facility in Pune, 
which will become operational in Q2 of FY 2028. We have also acquired the balance 9.9% 
equity stake in Walter Pack India, making it a wholly owned subsidiary of SJS Enterprises. With 
full ownership, Walter Pack is consolidating three Ranjangaon plants into one large facility for 
efficiency and growth, and it is expected to commence operations by May 2027. 
We will continue to align these additions and customer programs and maintain discipline through 
commissioning and ramp-up. Innovation remains at the heart of our product development, as 
aesthetic products increasingly combine visual appeal with technology. Our collaboration with 
BOE Varitronix is building our capabilities in optical cover glass, glass coatings and automotive 
electronic display systems, addressing the growing demand for digital displays in passenger 
vehicles. Combined with illuminated logos and a growing suite of advanced aesthetic products, 
these offerings significantly increase our content per vehicle and strengthen our standing with 
the OEMs as a capable, innovation-led partner for their new vehicle launches. 
During the quarter, we won several new businesses from TVS, Mahindra & Mahindra, Hero 
MotoCorp, Stellantis, Maruti Suzuki, Bajaj Auto, Royal Enfield, Whirlpool, Godrej, amongst 
others. SJS Decoplast added Tata Motors as a chrome plating customer, further increasing our 
cross-selling opportunities across the SJS portfolio. We also added HARMAN and TADME, 
which is Toyota Middle East, as our new customers and secured export orders from global OEMs 
like Stellantis, Whirlpool in North America, and TADME, Toyota Middle East. Exports grew 
23.1% year-on-year to Rs. 282.5 million. We are strengthening our presence in ASEAN, Europe, 
North America, and expanding into Turkey, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, South Korea, and 
Germany. Our engagements with several large global OEMs are progressing well, and we see 
promising opportunities ahead. We remain confident of achieving our 14%-15% export revenue 
share by FY 2028. 
During the period, we received several awards for financial management, customer engagement, 
and sustainability, and we continue to invest in employee development and manufacturing 
excellence. On sustainability, we began sourcing 2 MW of wind power from DB Renews Private 

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
Limited. We also joined the UN Global Compact, reinforcing our commitment to its 10 
principles and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. 
Through our CSR initiatives in sports, healthcare, education, and women’s empowerment, we 
supported 25 individuals with artificial knee replacements through Karnataka Marwari Youth 
Foundation and partnered with Sikshana Foundation on foundational literacy and numeracy 
programs across 50 government schools in Kanakapura, benefiting about 3,800 students. 
SJS believes in women empowerment, be it within the company or outside. Women now 
represent 17% of SJS workforce, up from 12% in FY 2022, reflecting our continued commitment 
in building a more diverse and inclusive organization. Extending this commitment to 
community, we partnered with Varchass Seva Trust to launch a Women Empowerment Project 
at Agara Panchayat, Bangalore, training 200 women in tailoring and beautician skills to help 
them build sustainable livelihoods. 
Looking ahead on the business front, we remain focused on premiumization, exports, and deeper 
customer relationships with disciplined execution, financial flexibility, and visibility from new 
programs. We are confident of delivering profitable growth and long-term value for all 
shareholders. 
With that, I hand over to Mahendra Naredi, our Group CFO, to take you through the financial 
performance. Over to you, Mahendra. 
Mahendra Naredi: 
Thank you, Sanjay sir, and good morning, everyone. Q2FY2027 has been another milestone 
quarter for SJS, with record quarterly revenue and profitability. 
Let me take you through our financial performance and key operating metrics: 
Starting with revenue, our revenue grew by 16.9% year-on-year to Rs. 2,827.3 million, our 
highest-ever quarterly revenue. An important milestone was achieved in September when our 
monthly revenue crossed Rs. 1,000 million for the first time in our history. Growth was primarily 
driven by passenger vehicle and exports. 
Moving to profitability, Gross profit grew by 17.9% to Rs. 1,597.3 million, with gross margin 
improving to 56.5% despite higher raw material, crude price, and startup costs. EBITDA grew 
by 23.1% to Rs. 896.4 million, with margins improving by 144 basis points to 31%, both record 
quarterly performance. The improvement was driven by higher exports, a favorable product mix, 
operational efficiencies, and our conscious decision to exit low-margin products at WPI. PAT 
grew by 34.8% to Rs. 583.3 million, with a margin of 20.6%, the highest normalized quarterly 
PAT margin since listing. Overall, profitability is growing significantly faster than revenue, 
reflecting healthy operating leverages. 

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
Coming to H1FY2027 performance, revenue grew by 20.4% to Rs. 5,437.3 million, while 
EBITDA grew by 28.9% to Rs. 1,696.0 million, with a margin of 30.5%. Reported PAT stood 
at Rs. 1,327.5 million, including a one-time gain of Rs. 241.7 million from the sale of our old 
Bangalore facility. Excluding this gain, underlying PAT grew by 39.4% to Rs. 1,085.8 million. 
Moving to cash flows and capital expenditure, cash generation continues to be strong, with H1 
cash flow from operations at Rs. 1,070.5 million and free cash flow at Rs. 1,077.3 million. Our 
total capex plan for FY 2026 to FY 2028 is Rs. 2,700 million to Rs. 2,850 million, covering our 
chrome plating and painting plant, SJS Bangalore capacity expansion, our display and cover 
glass plant, maintenance capex, and WPI plant consolidation. We have incurred Rs. 1,310.6 
million so far, including Rs. 822 million in FY 2026 and Rs. 488.6 million in H1 FY 2027. Our 
chrome plating and Bangalore projects are now largely complete, and the remaining capex will 
be funded entirely through internal accruals. 
During the quarter, we also acquired the remaining 9.9% stake in Walter Pack India for Rs. 
199.22 million, making WPI a wholly-owned subsidiary of SJS. Despite these investments and 
acquisition, we ended September with net cash of Rs. 3,318.7 million compared with Rs. 2,437 
million at the end of March 2026. 
Coming to return ratios, ROCE improved to 41.5% compared with 35.5% in FY 2026, while 
ROE improved to 22.8% compared with 20%. This improvement reflects better profitability, 
high utilization of existing capacities, tight working capital management, and a debt-free balance 
sheet. Importantly, we are delivering the ROE while maintaining substantial net cash equivalent 
to approximately one-third of shareholders' equity. Our financial strength is also reflected in 
ICRA AA- rating with a positive outlook. 
Finally, on our business mix and export, in Q2, passenger vehicle contributed 43.3% of revenue, 
two-wheeler 38.9%, and consumer and others contributed 17.8%. New generation products 
contributed 24% of total revenue. Exports grew by 23.1% to Rs. 282.5 million during Q2, 
contributing 10% of revenue. H1 export growth was even stronger at 45.8%. We remain on track 
to achieve our target of 14%-15% export contribution. 
To sum up, SJS continued to deliver healthy growth, record margins, and improving return 
ratios. We are generating strong cash flows, maintaining a robust net cash position, and funding 
our growth investments entirely through internal accruals. With most of our plant capacity 
investment now in place, we are well-positioned to sustain our growth momentum and create 
long-term shareholder value. 
With that, I hand over to Sanjay sir to take you through the business outlook and opportunity 
ahead. Over to you, sir. Thank you. 
Sanjay Thapar: 
Thank you, Mahendra. 

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
Moving on to outlook; As we enter H2FY2027, we remain confident of delivering profitable 
growth ahead of the automotive industry, supported by a differentiated business model, 
diversified product portfolio, and long-standing OEM relationships. Our priorities remain 
unchanged: increasing content per vehicle, building mega accounts, and converting new 
programs into revenue while maintaining operational efficiency and financial discipline. 
Innovation remains key to us, central to our strategy. We continue to develop advanced solutions, 
including optical cover glass, automotive displays, illuminated logos, and in-mold electronics. 
Exports remains a key priority, and we are targeting 14%-15% of consolidated revenue from 
exports by FY 2028, driven by deeper engagement with global customers, new program wins, 
and entry into new markets. 
SJS is expanding capacity with new and consolidated facilities at Pune and Bengaluru, mostly 
coming online in calendar year 2027, positioning the company to meet rising demand and 
support future growth. Our strong balance sheet, cash generation enable us to fund these 
investments while evaluating acquisitions that add complementary products, technologies, or 
customers. In a volatile environment marked by elevated commodity prices, subdued sentiment, 
pricing pressure across the industry has intensified to some extent and dampened consumer 
sentiment, resulting in dropping sales for consumer OEMs. 
In addition, the growth divergence between scooters and motorcycles within the two-wheeler 
industry continues to widen, and our portfolio is predominantly weighted towards motorcycles 
with relatively limited exposure to scooters. In light of the global macroeconomic environment, 
we have recalibrated our FY 2027 revenue growth outlook to 1.2x-1.5x of the growth of the 
passenger vehicle and motorcycle industry from 1.5x-2x earlier. 
At the same time, we continue focus on driving cost efficiencies and an improving product mix 
gives us the confidence to raise our EBITDA margin guidance to 29%-30% from 27%-28% 
earlier. This moderation reflects a deliberate strategic recalibration rather than a retreat. By 
consciously stepping back from select low-margin opportunities, we are positioning the business 
for stronger and more profitable growth ahead. 
Before concluding, I wish you and your families a very happy and prosperous Diwali. With that 
said, I come to an end of my quarterly updates. Thank you, and we are now open to answer 
questions. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. The first question 
is from the line of Chandramouli from Goldman Sachs.  
Chandramouli Muthiah: 
Hi, good morning, and thank you for taking my questions. My first question is just for a little bit 
of additional clarity on the growth outlook. Over the past 48 hours, it looks like a lot of sentiment 
seems to be changing around what might happen to crude oil prices and what might happen to 

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
metal costs. So, in that context, if there is a wave of correction in some of these input costs and 
crude oil prices correct, there could be some second derivative benefit on pricing as well as 
volume growth in the underlying industries that you serve. Just in the context of that, maybe this 
is premature, maybe it is not, but just wanted to understand what you think could be some of the 
upside optionality to this recalibrated outlook for the back half? 
Sanjay Thapar: 
Mr. Chandramouli, thank you for that question. Let me put that in proper perspective. So, at SJS, 
we are committed to allocate manufacturing resources to the most profitable businesses that we 
see for ourselves. As you are aware, in the last two quarters, we were almost operating at 
maximum capacity. So, this strategy for us was that what can we use our manufacturing 
resources to generate the best-in-class revenues and improve our already strong track record in 
terms of profitability, and we've done that, and that shows in the numbers. So, our EBITDA has 
grown to a record 31.0%, and essentially what we see with commodity prices easing, hopefully, 
let's hope that crude comes down and all the other commodities come down, that should improve 
buying sentiment. So, the segment that we address, the four-wheelers, the two-wheelers, the 
consumer businesses, the consumer especially is driven largely by sentiment, and this is 
something that we think will benefit from this macroeconomic future becoming a little more 
clearer. So, we expect that growth will come back, but essentially within SJS, we now have 
capacities in place to again restart or turbocharge our exports and our domestic business, and 
that should lead to higher growth. 
So we see that over the next few quarters, revenue should come back on trajectory. So, from 
what we said was allocation of resources to profitable products to increase our EBITDA, we will 
now be driving growth along with that, thanks to this tailwind of improved sentiment. I think 
it'll be positive not only for us, for the overall economy, and that is a very positive for the entire 
economy per se. 
Chandramouli Muthiah: 
Got it. Thank you. That's helpful. Second question is just around Tata and Stellantis. I think in 
recent quarters, you've been winning more business from Tata Motors, and Stellantis is one of 
the key customers which you think you can export more towards. And over the past few weeks, 
there have been announcements from both those entities around expanding the scope of their 
partnership and potentially sharing more vehicle platforms. So, as a supplier to Tata locally and 
Stellantis globally, just want to understand what you're seeing in potential opportunity size from 
that expanded scope and partnership between these two key customers? 
Sanjay Thapar: 
We have extremely strong relationship with both. Stellantis, the business continues to grow. 
We've won new export orders from Stellantis for a new category of products, which is decals. 
They have a lot of vehicles in the U.S., and we are making steady inroads into grabbing more 
and more share. With Tata, of course, we've been traditionally very, very strong for all the 
products that we have. We were, as I said, to the point of repeating, a little low on capacity, 
which has now come on track. So, we have a brand new plant for SJS Decoplast. We have 

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
increased capacity at SJS Bangalore. We are consolidating and increasing capacity at Walter 
Pack. So, we see these great opportunities to scale up the business very rapidly. 
So, essentially, the theme that we have is that customer support is critical. We need to be sure 
that we are able to deliver to customer expectation if we take an order. We have been circumspect 
that let us build capacity first before we target new customers. With now the capacity which is 
being done across all our plants, we are absolutely back in business, and we see a very strong 
trajectory for revenue growth coming from not only this partnership, but for all other customers 
as well. 
Chandramouli Muthiah: 
Got it. That's helpful. Last question is just around margin, and just related question on D&A. 
Could you just clarify in little more detail which are some of the lower-margin products that you 
look to do less of going forward, and what sort of products you're trying to vacate that capacity 
for? Also just related to that, we've had, I think, four successive quarters of depreciation 
reducing. So, just want to understand what's driving that and where that line item should settle 
out going forward. 
Sanjay Thapar: 
So, I will answer the question on product margins, and I will ask Mahendra to talk to you about 
depreciation. So, product margins, we have pruned in the last two quarters. We already have 
pruned the business, and in fact, in one case, we returned a large consumer business because we 
found that it was not giving us the margin that we wanted to. We won a successor business, 
which was a very high-margin business. Unfortunately, the war in West Asia dampened that 
requirement, so that export business was impacted, which I think now should come back with 
improving sentiment. So, our product portfolio has been sanitized, and we are a high-profit 
product mix across all the businesses that we do. So, all the pruning that had to happen has 
already happened, and that is the result where you see our margins to be extremely strong, and 
they will become stronger when we increase, let's say, benefit from the softening raw material 
prices. 
Mahendra, could you take that question on depreciation, please? 
Mahendra Naredi: 
Yes. Chandramouli, the depreciation for the quarter, we had Rs.108.9 million, which is lower 
than the last quarter. When we acquired the Walter Pack, some intangible was recorded, and 
after the period of three years, this impact is now nullifying. This is starting from the Q2FY2027. 
So, approximately Rs.10 million is impacted there. Because of that, the depreciation amount has 
come down. And we have capitalized this SJS Decoplast, the Pune facility, and the Bangalore 
facility in this quarter. The full impact will start from the Q3. So, that will going to start in next 
quarter, and we will have an increased depreciation starting from Q3. 
Chandramouli Muthiah: 
Got it. That's helpful. Thank you very much. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Ajox Frederick from Sundaram Mutual Fund.  

 
SJS Enterprises Limited 
November 05, 2026 
 
Ajox Frederick: 
Hi, sir. Thanks for the opportunity. So, first question is on exports. So, what are the low-hanging 
fruits or the visibility or even the type of businesses we are closer to winning in the next, let's 
say, one year to 18 months timeframe? That's one. Secondly is, will acquisition be a route for 
enhancing our exports, let's say, to acquire a particular customer etc.? So, it's an export-related 
question plus acquisition, anything on works, anything being discussed, more on those lines, sir. 
Sanjay Thapar: 
Okay. The low-hanging fruit and exports really are, we've cross-selling of products to the 
existing customers. Stellantis was a very major customer we acquired. As I mentioned earlier, 
we won business for decals with Stellantis. The opportunity set is even larger, but typically what 
these companies do is test you on a program and then once they see that, yes, development is on 
time, they open doors to more products. So, cross-selling to export customers more product from 
our portfolio is one low-hanging fruit. The other one is chrome plating. There was a lot of pent-
up demand, and that is the reason why we expanded this, set up this new plant for chrome plating. 
We see a lot of mega inquiries for chrome plating. At the moment, we are in the negotiation

remain relevant to the emerging infrastructure opportunities, particularly in technology-enabled 
infrastructure and allied sector. We have already entered in new areas such as smart meters and

activities to be undertaken by the company.

over the call to Director (Finance) for his opening comments.
Devendra Kumar: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, valued investors, analysts and
members of the media. Thank you for joining MRPL's Q2 FY 2026-27 earnings call. Allow me to take you
through the quarter's results and a few key updates before we open the floor.
As you all know, the industry, especially the refining industry, is going through challenging times due to
geopolitical situations mainly arising out of the conflict in West Asia. This has resulted in a squeezing of
assured supplies from the Middle East, longer voyage times and a steep increase in freight and insurance
costs. The industry is still in reactionary mode and events are evolving on a regular basis. The company
continues to navigate these challenging times with professionalism and determination while maintaining
its nation-first approach.
Moving to performance, the company's Q2 performance was relatively strong. The standalone net profit
was %1,881 crore on an EBITDA base of %3,210 crore. This is nearly three times the profit of Q2 of last
year, which stood at %639 crore. This has been achieved despite a planned shutdown in August. The
throughput was 4.18 MMT during Q2 against a quarterly peak of about 4.5 MMT achieved earlier. The
fuel and loss stood at 9.86% for H1, compared to around 11% reported earlier.
MRPL ~ Q2 FY 2026-27 Earnings Conference Call Transcript Page 1

FQ
For the half year, the net profit is %2,796 crore against 2367 crore for the corresponding H1 of the previous
year. Considering the positive performance for H1 ofthis year, the Board has declared an interim dividend
of 33 per share, which works out to a total dividend of 3526 crore. Borrowings fell by over 35,000 crore in
six months, reaching %9,245 crore at the end of September. This is, of course, variable and depends on
working capital requirements. The debt-equity ratio has correspondingly improved from 1.01 as reported
at the end of March 2026 to 0.55 at the end of September 2026.
Moving on to our crude sourcing: despite the West Asia disruptions, the company has kept crude supplies
secure by diversifying its crude sourcing basket. When Middle East term cargoes were curtailed by the
situation in the Strait of Hormuz, we stepped up domestic crude and spot purchases. In Q2, domestic
crude made up about a quarter of our intake, term contracts about a fifth, and spot purchases the balance,
drawn mainly from West Africa, the Americas, the Middle East and Russia. Russian barrels made up about
32% of our Q2 basket, against approximately 28% in Q1. Every cargo is procured on commercial terms,
decided on delivered economics.
Moving on, our retail network has 257 retail outlets across Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and, lately,
Andhra Pradesh. The half-yearly retail margin continued to be marginally negative. The capex for financial
year 2026-27 is expected to be in the range of %1,200 crore to 21,500 crore, which includes refinery
maintenance, revamping, and small-value IRR projects including retail projects.
Moving on to the major events during the half year: there was the formation ofa JV company, OPML, that
is, ONGC Petrochemicals Marketing Limited, with a 50% stake held by ONGC, 25% by OPal and 25% by
MRPL. MRPL's investment will be to the tune of %12.5 crore. This JV is formed for marketing of
petrochemicals and related products. It is expected to enhance the petrochemical business and
operational planning, and reduce costs through improved logistics, warehousing, grade optimisation and
customer management.
PNGRB has granted authorisation to MRPL for laying, building, operating or expanding a petroleum and
petroleum products (ATF) pipeline from Devanagonthi to Bengaluru airport. This is expected to be
completed by the year 2029-30 at a cost of ¥200 crore plus.
For the first time, MRPL has been able to obtain an international credit rating. Fitch International has
assigned a rating of BBB- (Stable), which is at par with the sovereign rating and comparable with its peer
companies and OMCs.
There was a long-pending tax case, and we have been able to close that long-pending reformate
classification dispute. We have received a refund of %212 crore.
The company has won two National Innovation Awards at the recently concluded 29th Energy Technology
and Innovation Meet, that is, ETM 2026, held at Goa. These achievements reinforce the company's
commitment to R&D and innovation and support the Government of India's vision of Aatmanirbhar
Bharat.
On the flip side, there was a fire incident on 30th September 2026 at around noon at our Coker
Hydrotreater Unit (CHTU). The incident is under active investigation and reconstruction of the unit has
commenced. Restoration is targeted by mid-December
this year, and we expect Q3 throughput to be close
to Q2 levels. We have booked a provisional loss of 3118.76 crore in Q2 as an exceptional item, against an
MRPL - Q2 FY 2026-27 Earnings Conference Call Transcript Page 2

estimated replacement value of about 225 crore. These are, of course, preliminary estimates. The assets
are adequately insured.
To sum up, MRPL continues to follow a nation-first approach, which was evident from MRPL's ramping up
of LPG supplies by cutting down on polypropylene during H1. We will continue to strive to keep
throughput and product supplies at the peak levels technically possible for fulfilling domestic demand
first. We are targeting a retail presence of about 500 retail outlets by the end of FY 2028. We continue to
follow a balanced portfolio approach of debt reduction, modest capex and shareholder returns. Based on
current market conditions and performance trends, the company is expected to continue to maintain a
strong balance sheet in the current year.
